The measured fidelity agrees with our error model dominated by atomic motion, indicating a straightforward route to higher fidelity through improved cooling, while the fundamental error contribution from Rydberg decay is below $3\times10^{-4}$. These results establish a path to entangling-gate fidelities substantially beyond the current state of the art through cryogenic suppression of Rydberg decay, reducing the overhead for fault-tolerant computation.
item.dc:creator: Junlan Jin, Donghyuk Seo, Yue Shi, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, Waseem S. Bakr

item.title: Local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40337v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider bulk-gapped fermion systems whose infinite-volume bulk is obtained by adding sufficiently weak even many-body interactions to a free Hamiltonian with spectral gap $g>0$, allowing polynomial spatial decay of both parts. We prove quantitative local determination of low-energy states: whenever another interaction agrees with the bulk interaction inside a finite or infinite region $U$, with bulk terms crossing its boundary unchanged or removed, all its states with excitation energies in $[0,3g/4]$ have local expectations close to those of the bulk ground state deep inside $U$. The error decays with the distance to the complement of $U$, independently of the interaction terms supported outside $U$ and of the chosen low-energy state. Quantitative local determination has strong consequences. (i) The bulk interaction has a unique algebraic ground state. (ii) A strong "local perturbations perturb locally" (LPPL) principle holds: arbitrary distant defects change local ground-state expectations only by a spatially decaying error. (iii) Low-energy excitations in finite samples remain localized near the boundary for all times, up to spatially decaying tails, uniformly over arbitrary even boundary terms. (iv) Correlations from deep inside $U$ to outside $U$ are small, with quantitative bounds in terms of spatial separation and distance to $U^c$. To prove local determination of low-energy states, we combine quasi-adiabatic transport of the free ground state to the interacting bulk ground state with a new condition, local excitation detectability (LED). A companion paper establishes gap stability and constructs the transport for weak interactions, while we prove LED at sufficiently weak coupling. The abstract theorem is nonperturbative and applies whenever the transport and LED hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Teufel

item.title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
item.description: arXiv:2610.40353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schr\"odinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable. The general revival subject acquires a far greater complexity in the bosonic many-body context that offers a larger variety of observables and intrinsically implies high dimensionality. Here, the focus is on the simplest nontrivial (i.e., not 1D) bosonic many-body system, namely a symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model. The non-equilibrium situation of a coherent initial state prepared on one of the two sites of this integrable 2D system in the strongly self-trapping regime is considered. The revival behaviors emerging from the resulting dynamics within expectation values, coherences, and the autocorrelation function are theoretically derived, and the entanglement behavior is illustrated. Several new features, unknown so far in the Schr\"odinger context and identified here in terms of five ``puzzles'', are encountered and discussed, among them, a synchronized resurgence behavior, differing revivals times depending on the specific observable, and a manifestation of a precession that appears in the underlying mean field dynamics. These new phenomena can be entirely understood through a comprehensive semiclassical theory, building upon the underlying classical (mean-field) phase-space structure. A quantitative comparison of the latter with semiclassical predictions and quantum perturbative calculations yields an overall excellent agreement and confirms that a full semiclassical theory is pivotal for the understanding of these genuinely quantum many-body interference phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Denis Ullmo (LPTMS, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay / CNRS, Orsay), Steven Tomsovic (LPTMS, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay / CNRS, Orsay, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Washington State University, Pullman), Gabriel M. Lando (LPTMS, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay / CNRS, Orsay), Peter Schlagheck (CESAM research unit, University of Liege, Liege)

item.title: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities
item.description: arXiv:2610.40402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Polaritonic chemistry holds the promise of controlling chemical reactivity through confined light-matter interactions, yet how reactions respond inside optical cavities remains debated. Here, we take a more zoomed-out view, inspired by electrostatic catalysis. We extend nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to cavity-modified reactions and show that their behavior falls into four distinct reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions can follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior regardless of cavity tuning, or switch between the two as the cavity frequency is varied. We establish this picture analytically and demonstrate it in the Shin Metiu model and in four molecular reactions treated with ab initio electronic-structure methods. Even at this deliberately coarse-grained level, cavity-modified reactivity already shows qualitatively different and strongly counterintuitive behavior, including reactions that switch character with cavity frequency. Yet this complexity can still be reduced to a simple competition between permanent-dipole and polarizability responses. This reaction-type classification therefore provides a new route to organize and anticipate cavity-modified reactivity.
item.dc:creator: Jillian G. Hoffstadt, Davis M. Welakuh, Norah M. Hoffmann

item.title: Micromagnetic Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Normal-Mode Formulation of Cavity Magnon-Photon Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate magnon-photon interactions in a resonant cavity starting from the coupled Maxwell and Landau-Lifshitz equations linearized about an arbitrary micromagnetic ground state. By introducing an electric vector potential and a suitable interaction Lagrangian, the formulation avoids the cancellation of large magnetostatic contributions that arises in the conventional magnetic-vector-potential description and becomes inaccurate under modal truncation. The magnetization and cavity fields are expanded in the normal modes of the uncoupled magnetic and electromagnetic subsystems, with coupling coefficients given by overlap integrals of the corresponding eigenfunctions. The resulting multimode Lagrangian has a noncanonical structure due to the gyrotropic terms, and the corresponding Hamiltonian formulation is obtained using the Faddeev-Jackiw approach. The radiative magnon-photon interaction is encoded in the resulting Poisson-bracket structure, while the cavity-induced modification of the magnetostatic field enters explicitly in the Hamiltonian. The coupled system is diagonalized through a generalized Bogoliubov transformation, yielding canonical polariton variables that provide a natural basis for quantization. Application to a perpendicularly magnetized YIG disk in a rectangular microwave cavity shows hybridization between the cavity mode and several magnetostatic modes, together with appreciable cavity-wall-induced frequency shifts when the sample is placed close to the conducting walls.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Serpico, Marco Lembo, Giovanni Miano

item.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.40423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. We interpret these findings with ab initio calculations and an effective spin-circuit model that reproduces the anisotropic magnetotransport. Our results identify the displacement field as an efficient electrical control parameter of spin transport in CrSBr and suggest that multi-gate architectures could provide similar control in other layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Soliman, Jaime Garrido Aldea, Davy Borowski, Dorye L. Esteras, Neeraj K. Rajak, Niels Chapuis, Abdelkarim Ouerghi, Arnaud Gloppe, J\'er\^ome Robert, Bernard Doudin, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Jos\'e H. Garc\'ia, Stephan Roche, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Dayen

item.title: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.40460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a static dipolar impurity immersed in a Fermi gas and show how dipolar interactions shape both the few-body scattering properties and the resulting polaron physics. Using Fumi's theorem, we connect the anisotropic phase shifts directly to the ground-state energy, and compute the exact impurity spectrum via the functional determinant approach. The resulting spectrum is a convolution of independent even- and odd-wave contributions, giving rise to a ground state with simultaneously occupied even- and odd-wave bound states whose separation is tunable via the dipole length. A variational ansatz limited to one particle-hole excitation fails to capture this doubly occupied ground state. We further find that long-range dipolar interactions weaken Anderson's orthogonality catastrophe, reducing the power-law decay of the quasiparticle weight. These effects can be tested with ultracold polar molecules, where microwave shielding and independent tunability of interactions enable experimental access to the predicted regimes.
item.dc:creator: Eugen Dizer, Xin Chen, Richard Schmidt, Arthur Christianen

item.title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
item.description: arXiv:2610.40463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoist, Laurent Bruneau, Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Aannalisa Panati, Claude-Alain Pillet

item.title: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.40523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. The correction term, arising from consistent incorporation of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality, restores gauge invariance and makes it possible to separate the total angular momentum into spin and orbital components. We propose a method for calculating the orbital and spin angular momenta of multimode vector vortex fields and show that the orbital angular momentum of such beams contains two qualitatively different components. The polarization-independent contribution to the orbital angular momentum is related to the topological charge that determines the order of the phase singularity, while the polarization-dependent one is proportional to the helical topological charge that determines the spatial inhomogeneity of the polarization. We also discuss the quantization procedure for fields with spatially inhomogeneous polarization in terms of modes with a helical topological charge, and examine the limits of applicability of the proposed formalism.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Maliutina, E. A. Vashukevich, V. A. Leonov, D. D. Reshetnikov, T. Yu. Golubeva

item.title: Quasi-Phases of Quantum Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.40526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Within quantum many-body phase diagrams, continuous transition lines can appear and then terminate. However, it has remained unclear whether the neighboring regimes can be meaningfully described as distinct phases, akin to water and vapour, since any sharp characterization would have to go beyond the usual notion of phases of matter. We answer this in the affirmative by introducing quasi-phases: gapped regimes near a critical point that are connected in the broader phase diagram, but not by any gapped path accessible from small perturbations of the critical theory. The physical consequences include interface modes between regimes in the same phase of matter. More striking still, describing both the extended critical line and the gapped path connecting the regimes requires a bigger multicritical parent theory. In spin-chain examples with continuous terminating lines with central charge $c=1$, we find multicritical $c=3/2$ and $c=9/5$ orbifolds describing so-called 'quotient symmetry protected' and 'representation symmetry protected' topological phenomena. While one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases are labeled by projective representation classes, these quasi-phases can have interface modes carrying higher-dimensional linear representations. We turn this into a constructive principle through a weakening of the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomaly. Supporting distinct quasi-phases makes an unnecessary critical point infrared-necessary, even if it is unnecessary at the ultraviolet scale. This condition is more restrictive than simply having a codimension-one critical line, revealing richer structure within phases of matter than their conventional classification suggests.
item.dc:creator: Nick G. Jones, Paul Fendley, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Ruben Verresen

item.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
item.description: arXiv:2610.40589v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An autonomous research laboratory could conduct an entire study, from formulating questions to preparing manuscripts. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers one route towards this goal. Recent AI systems take on several research roles, but may draw conclusions that the evidence does not support. Here, we present an autonomous research laboratory in which agents based on large language models assess one another's work and can stop or redirect investigations. They can generate and reject research questions, require separate theoretical checks and conduct experiments designed to challenge their claims. We demonstrate these capabilities by investigating ensembles of quantum spins in diamond. The agents derived the minimum number of calibration settings needed to predict responses to a defined family of microwave pulse sequences. They checked the result computationally and designed experiments to distinguish competing predictions. An initial experiment agreed with the theoretical predictions, but repeated reference measurements showed that the signal was drifting during data collection. The agents therefore treated the result as inconclusive and revised the measurement protocol without relaxing the acceptance criteria. The revised experiment met those criteria and supported the theoretical predictions. This study demonstrates that collaborating AI agents can select research questions, derive theoretical results and test their predictions experimentally.
item.dc:creator: El Mustapha Mansouri, Eikichi Kimura, Masato Koga, Keigo Arai

item.title: Algebraic theory of abelian fractons and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.40596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of fusion, mobility, and statistics in abelian gapped fracton orders and topological phases. The framework generalizes the algebraic description of abelian anyons to systems with restricted-mobility and spatially extended excitations. We consider translation-invariant bosonic systems whose pointlike and extended excitations have finite fusion order. The basic objects are braided fusion complexes (BFCs): chain complexes encoding fusion and mobility, equipped with a braiding chain map encoding statistics. Their equivalence classes define braided fusion theories (BFTs). Our framework encompasses arbitrary translation-invariant Pauli codes, as well as all abelian anyon theories in two spatial dimensions, including chiral theories. We give evidence for the conjecture that every nondegenerate BFT can be realized as the excitation theory of a gapped phase and that the BFT describing such a phase is a phase invariant. We derive constraints on pointlike fusion and mobility, showing, for example, that neither the Pauli X nor Z sectors of the X-cube and anisotropic models can occur alone in a nondegenerate BFT. For nondegenerate theories with only pointlike excitations, we extract a simpler theory of mutual statistics, consisting of a fusion module and a map to its statistical dual. This theory of mutual statistics is an invariant of the BFT and, at odd fusion order, gives an equivalent description of the full braided fusion theory. We interpret remote detection as the generalization of mutual statistics to fracton orders. In the BFC setting, we give a precise formulation of the excitation-detector principle: every nontrivial excitation can be detected by an operator supported at spatial infinity, and every nontrivial detector detects some excitation. Assuming a unique infinite-space ground state, we prove that this principle is equivalent to nondegeneracy.
item.dc:creator: Wilbur Shirley, Evan Wickenden, Bowen Yang, Agn\`es Beaudry, Michael Hermele

item.title: Renormalization for Robust Memory without Synchronization
item.description: arXiv:2610.40651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local error correction can preserve classical information against noise, but protection under synchronized updates need not survive when sites evolve at independent random times. Establishing stability is particularly challenging when protection relies on the collective action of competing local rules. Here we develop a spacetime renormalization framework that reveals how independently acting local updates can collectively stabilize memory. We identify sufficient conditions under which the geometry of stable interfaces and suppression of defect propagation produce reliable erosion at large scales. Applying this framework, we prove stability of the asynchronous \textsf{R} squeezing code and introduce robust processes in two and three dimensions. In these systems, both encoded phases persist under sufficiently weak noise, even when the noise favors one phase. Our results provide a criterion for designing autonomous memories sustained by competing local stochastic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Chakraborty, Jong Yeon Lee

item.title: A quantum central path algorithm for linear optimization
item.description: arXiv:2311.03977v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a novel quantum algorithm for solving linear optimization problems by quantum-mechanical simulation of the central path. While interior point methods follow the central path with an iterative algorithm that works with successive linearizations of the perturbed KKT conditions, we perform a simulation working directly with the nonlinear complementarity equations. Using a two-stage quantum eigenpath traversal schedule, this approach yields an algorithm for solving linear optimization problems involving $m$ constraints and $n$ variables to $\varepsilon$-optimality using $\widetilde{O}\!\left((m+n)^{3/2}\,\varepsilon^{-1}+(m+n)^{1/2}\,\varepsilon^{-3/2}\right)$ queries to an oracle that evaluates a potential function. In the standard gate model (i.e., without access to quantum RAM), our algorithm can obtain $\varepsilon$-precise solutions to LO problems using at most $$\widetilde{O}\!\left(\left[\frac{(m+n)^{3/2}}{\varepsilon} + \frac{(m+n)^{1/2}}{\varepsilon^{3/2}}\right] \cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A)\right)$$ elementary gates, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the total number of non-zero elements found in the constraint matrix.
item.dc:creator: Brandon Augustino, Jiaqi Leng, Jialu Bao, Giacomo Nannicini, Tam\'as Terlaky, Xiaodi Wu

item.title: Security of hybrid BB84 with heterodyne detection
item.description: arXiv:2402.16941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) promises everlasting security based on the laws of physics. Most common protocols are grouped into two distinct categories based on the degrees of freedom used to carry information, which can be either discrete or continuous, each presenting unique advantages in either performance, feasibility for near-term implementation, and compatibility with existing telecommunications architectures. Recently, hybrid QKD protocols have been introduced to leverage advantages from both categories. In this work we provide a rigorous security proof for a protocol introduced by Qi in 2021, where information is encoded in discrete variables as in the widespread Bennett Brassard 1984 protocol but decoded continuously via heterodyne detection. Security proofs for hybrid protocols inherit the same challenges associated with continuous-variable protocols due to unbounded dimensions. Here we successfully address these challenges by exploiting symmetry. Our approach enables truncation of the Hilbert space with precise control of the approximation errors and lead to a tight, semi-analytical expression for the asymptotic key rate under collective attacks. As concrete examples, we apply our theory to compute the key rates under passive attacks, linear loss, and Gaussian noise.
item.dc:creator: Jasminder S. Sidhu, Rocco Maggi, Saverio Pascazio, Cosmo Lupo

item.title: Conditional Motional Squeezing of an Optomechanical Oscillator Approaching the Quantum Regime
item.description: arXiv:2410.09208v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Squeezed mechanical states are a highly coveted resource for quantum-enhanced sensing and serve as a compelling platform for probing the interplay between gravity and quantum mechanics. It has been predicted that a mechanical oscillator can be prepared into a quantum squeezed state if the applied measurement rate is fast relative to its mechanical resonance frequency. However, the experimental feasibility of this protocol has remained uncertain because of the difficulty in achieving low-frequency oscillators with sufficiently strong read-out. Here, we demonstrate that a careful selection of parameters in an optomechanical system, combined with optimal filtering techniques, enables the preparation of a 50 ng GaAs cantilever in a conditional classical squeezed state, achieving a minimum uncertainty of just 1.07 plus/minus 0.04 times the zero-point fluctuation level. This minimum variance is 3 orders of magnitude smaller than what has been achieved in previous experiments using the same protocol. Although we do not fully achieve the quantum squeezed regime, our demonstration provides definitive evidence that a measurement-based protocol is a practical and effective approach for the real-time preparation of macroscopic oscillators in quantum squeezed states.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin B. Lane, Junxin Chen, Ronald E. Pagano, Scott Aronson, Garrett D. Cole, Xinghui Yin, Vivishek Sudhir, Thomas R. Corbitt, Nergis Mavalvala

item.title: Dissipative Dynamical Phase Transition as a Complex Ising Model
item.description: arXiv:2412.09591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a quantum dynamical phase transition induced by the competition between local unitary evolution and dissipation in a qubit chain with a strong, on-site $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. While the steady-state of this evolution is always maximally-mixed, we show that the dynamical behavior of certain non-local observables on the approach to this steady-state is dictated by a quantum Ising model with a complex transverse-field (cTFIM). A crucial feature of our mapping to the cTFIM is an extensive number of local, weak, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries possessed by the dynamics, allowing us to investigate these observables analytically and uncover a dynamical phase transition as the relative rate of unitary evolution and dissipation is tuned. We show that the weak-dissipation limit corresponds to a cTFIM with a large magnitude of the imaginary transverse-field, for which the many-body "ground-state" (with smallest real eigenvalue) is gapless, exhibiting quasi-long-range correlations of the local magnetization with a continuously-varying exponent. Correspondingly, the dynamics of the non-local observables show oscillatory behavior with an amplitude decaying exponentially in time. The strong-dissipation limit corresponds to a gapped ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, and non-local observables show exponential decay on the approach to equilibrium. This transition in (1+1)-dimensions has a peculiar, "two-sided" nature appearing as either first- or second-order depending on the phase from which the transition is approached, an analytic result which is corroborated by numerical studies. In higher dimensions, we present a field-theoretic understanding of the first-order nature of this transition, when approaching from the ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, though the nature of the phase with large imaginary transverse-field remains to be understood.
item.dc:creator: Stephen W. Yan, Diego Barberena, Matthew P. A. Fisher, Sagar Vijay

item.title: ShotQC: Reducing Sampling Overhead in Quantum Circuit Cutting
item.description: arXiv:2412.17704v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recently developed quantum circuit cutting technique greatly extends the capabilities of current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. However, it introduces substantial overhead in both classical postprocessing and quantum resources, as the postprocessing complexity and sampling cost scale exponentially with the number of circuit cuts. In this work, we propose an enhanced circuit cutting framework, ShotQC, which effectively reduces the sampling overhead through two key optimizations: shot distribution and cut parameterization. The former employs an adaptive Monte Carlo strategy to dynamically allocate more quantum shots to subcircuit configurations that contribute more to the variance in the final outcome. The latter exploits additional degrees of freedom in postprocessing to further suppress variance. Integrating these optimizations, ShotQC significantly reduces the sampling overhead without increasing classical postprocessing complexity, as demonstrated across a range of benchmark circuits.
item.dc:creator: Po-Hung Chen, Bo-Hung Chen, Dah-Wei Chiou, Jie-Hong Roland Jiang

item.title: Genetic algorithm enhanced Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for quantum compiling of Fibonacci anyons
item.description: arXiv:2501.01746v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum compiling, which aims to approximate target qubit gates by finding optimal sequences (braidwords) of basic braid operations, constitutes a fundamental challenge in quantum computing. We develop a genetic algorithm (GA)-enhanced Solovay--Kitaev algorithm (SKA) for approximating single-qubit gates using four elementary braiding matrices (EBMs) derived from Fibonacci anyons. The GA-enhanced SKA demonstrates robust performance, efficiently identifying optimal braidwords within exponentially large search spaces. Notably, the approximation precision achieved by our method surpasses that of Monte Carlo (MC)-enhanced SKA and becomes comparable to deep reinforcement learning (RL) approaches when braidword lengths exceed $25$. Implementing $2$- and $3$-order approximations with the GA-enhanced SKA yields optimal braidwords (with initial braiding lengths $l_{0} = 50$ and $l_{0} = 30$, respectively) achieving gate distances of $5.9 \times 10^{-7}$ --- sufficient precision for most quantum computing applications. This work develops an optimized compilation framework for non-Abelian anyon gates, providing an essential methodology for enhancing future topological quantum computation architectures through gate optimization.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwei Long, Xuyang Huang, Jianxin Zhong, Lijun Meng

item.title: Macroscopic quantum coherence and entanglement in mechanical systems
item.description: arXiv:2503.08324v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The notion of a macroscopic quantum state must be pinned down in order to assess how well experiments probe the large-scale limits of quantum mechanics. However, the issue of quantifying so-called quantum macroscopicity is fraught with multiple approaches having varying interpretations and levels of computability and measurability. Here, we introduce two measures that capture independent macroscopic properties: i) extensive size, measuring the degree of coherence in position or momentum observables relative to atomic-scale units, and ii) entangled size, quantifying the number of entangled subsystems. These measures unify many desirable features of past proposals while having rigorously justified interpretations from quantum information theory in terms of coherence and multipartite entanglement. We demonstrate how to estimate them and obtain lower-bounds using experimental data from micro-mechanical oscillators and diffracting molecules. Notably, we find evidence for genuine multipartite entanglement of $10^5$ to $10^7$ atoms in recent mechanical superposition states.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Yadin, Matteo Fadel

item.title: Classification of locality preserving symmetries on spin chains
item.description: arXiv:2503.15088v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the action of a finite group $G$ by locality preserving automorphisms (quantum cellular automata) on quantum spin chains. We refer to such group actions as ``symmetries''. The natural notion of equivalence for such symmetries is \emph{stable equivalence}, which allows for stacking with factorized group actions. Stacking also endows the set of equivalence classes with a group structure. We prove that the anomaly of such symmetries provides an isomorphism between the group of stable equivalence classes of symmetries with the cohomology group $H^3(G,U(1))$, consistent with previous conjectures. This amounts to a complete classification of locality preserving symmetries on spin chains.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Mathematical Physics, volume 407, issue 1 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Alex Bols, Wojciech De Roeck, Michiel De Wilde, Bruno de O. Carvalho

item.title: The construction of a universal quantum gate set for the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_k$ $(k = 5,\, 6,\, 7)$ anyon models via genetic optimized algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2505.01774v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We systematically study a numerical method for constructing a universal quantum gate set for topological quantum computation (TQC) using $\mathrm{SU}(2)_k$ anyon models. The $F$-matrices and $R$-symbols are computed through the $q$-deformed representation theory of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, enabling precise determination of elementary braiding matrices (EBMs) for $\mathrm{SU}(2)_k$ anyon systems. Quantum gates are derived from these EBMs. One-qubit gates are synthesized using a genetic algorithm-enhanced Solovay--Kitaev algorithm (GA-enhanced SKA), while two-qubit gates are constructed through brute-force search or GA optimization to approximate the local equivalence class $[\mathrm{CNOT}]$. Implementing this framework for the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_5$, $\mathrm{SU}(2)_6$, and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_7$ models successfully generates the canonical universal gate set $\{H\text{-gate},\ T\text{-gate},\ \mathrm{CNOT}\text{-gate}\}$. These numerical results provide conclusive verification of the universal quantum computation capabilities inherent in $\mathrm{SU}(2)_k$ anyon models. Furthermore, we obtain exact implementations of the local equivalence class $[\mathrm{SWAP}]$ using nine EBMs in each model.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwei Long, Yizhi Li, Jianxin Zhong, Lijun Meng

item.title: Tight Generalization of Robertson-Type Uncertainty Relations
item.description: arXiv:2505.19861v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the tightest possible Robertson-type preparation uncertainty relation, which explicitly depends on the eigenvalues of the quantum state. The conventional constant $ \tfrac{1}{4} $ is replaced by the state-dependent coefficient \[ \frac{(\lambda_{\max} + \lambda_{\min})^2}{4(\lambda_{\max} - \lambda_{\min})^2}, \] where $ \lambda_{\max} $ and $\lambda_{\min}$ denote the largest and smallest eigenvalues of the density operator $ \rho $, respectively. We prove that this coefficient is optimal among all Robertson-type generalizations and does not admit further improvement. We also obtain a complete characterization of all nontrivial equality cases. Our relation becomes more pronounced as the quantum state becomes more mixed, capturing a trade-off in quantum uncertainty that the conventional Robertson's relation fails to detect. In addition, our result also provides a strict generalization of the Schr\"odinger's uncertainty relation, showing that the uncertainty trade-off is governed by the sum of the covariance term and a state-dependent improvement over the Robertson bound. As applications, we also refine error-disturbance trade-offs by incorporating spectral information of both the system and the measuring apparatus, thereby generalizing the Arthurs-Goodman and Ozawa inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Gen Kimura, Aina Mayumi, Haruki Yamashita

item.title: Entanglement Scaling of Motzkin Chains under Spiral Hamiltonian-path Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2506.02103v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how a two-dimensional spatial embedding changes the entanglement observed across geometrically local bipartitions of a one-dimensional quantum spin chain. A $q$-deformed colored Motzkin chain is placed along a spiral-inspired Hamiltonian path that visits $N(L)=\Theta(L^2)$ sites of a square-lattice region while retaining a path interaction graph. Straight ambient-space cuts then correspond to unions of $\Theta(L)$ disconnected intervals in the chain ordering. We derive the scaling of a height-variation proxy for the leading color-pairing contribution and predict ambient-space entropy scaling proportional to $L^2$, $L$, and $O(1)$ for $q>1$, $q=1$, and $q<1$, respectively. We evaluate this proxy numerically using the matrix-product-state representation and verify its predicted finite-size scaling. The embedded and original Hamiltonians have exactly identical spectra and spectral gaps at fixed chain length. We also describe a sparse tensor-network representation and propose a two-chain junction extension. These results isolate the roles of interaction connectivity, spatial embedding, and subsystem geometry in entanglement scaling.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Zhang, Olai B. Mykland

item.title: Partitions in quantum theory
item.description: arXiv:2506.22218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Decompositional theories describe the ways in which a global physical system can be split into subsystems, facilitating the study of how different possible partitions of the same system interplay, e.g. in terms of inclusions or signalling. In quantum theory, subsystems are usually framed as sub-C*-algebras of the algebra of operators on the global system. However, most decompositional approaches have so far restricted their scope to the case of systems corresponding to factor algebras. We argue that this is a mistake: one should cater for the possibility for non-factor subsystems, arising for instance from symmetry considerations. Building on simple examples, we motivate and present a definition of partitions into an arbitrary number of parts, each of which is a possibly non-factor sub-C*-algebra. We discuss its physical interpretation and study its properties, in particular with regard to the structure of algebras' centres. We prove that partitions, defined at the C*-algebraic level, can be represented in terms of a splitting of Hilbert spaces, using the framework of routed quantum circuits. For some partitions, however, such a representation necessarily retains a residual pseudo-nonlocality. We provide an example of this behaviour, given by the partition of a fermionic system into local modes.
item.dc:creator: Augustin Vanrietvelde, Octave Mestoudjian, Pablo Arrighi

item.title: Brace for impact: ECDLP challenges for quantum cryptanalysis
item.description: arXiv:2508.14011v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Precise suites of benchmarks are required to assess the progress of early fault-tolerant quantum computers at economically impactful applications such as cryptanalysis. Appropriate challenges exist for factoring but those for elliptic curve cryptography are either too sparse or inadequate for standard applications of Shor's algorithm. We introduce a difficulty-graded suite of elliptic curve discrete logarithm (ECDLP) challenges that use Bitcoin's curve y^2=x^3+7 mod p while incrementally lowering the prime field from 256 down to 6 bits. For each bit-length, we provide the prime, the prime group order, and two deterministic nothing-up-my-sleeve (NUMS) points in compressed SEC1 form. All challenges are generated by a deterministic, reproducible procedure, and no private challenge scalar is chosen in advance. We calibrate classical cost against Pollard's rho records and quantum cost against resource estimation results for Shor's algorithm. We compile Shor's ECDLP circuit to logical counts and map them to physical resources for various parameters of the surface code, the repetition cat code and the LDPC cat codes. Under explicit and testable assumptions on physical error rates, code distances, and non-Clifford supply, our scenarios place the full 256-bit instance within a 2027--2033 window. The challenge ladder thus offers a transparent ruler to track fault-tolerant progress on a cryptanalytic target of immediate relevance, and it motivates proactive migration of digital assets to post-quantum signatures.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Luc Dallaire-Demers, William Doyle, Timothy Foo

item.title: Measurement-Based Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation on High-Connectivity Devices: A Resource-Efficient Approach toward Early FTQC
item.description: arXiv:2510.18652v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a measurement-based fault-tolerant quantum computing (MB-FTQC) architecture for high-connectivity platforms, targeting early-FTQC devices with thousands to tens of thousands of physical qubits. Unlike earlier teleportation-based architectures that rely on code concatenation for scalability, MB-FTQC operates in a zero-concatenation regime with compact fixed-distance codes, keeping the qubit overhead within reach of such devices. MB-FTQC combines offline-verified logical resource states with Knill's error-correcting teleportation, allowing each online step to use single-round syndrome extraction and independent lookup-table decoding. Under circuit-level depolarizing noise, we study a Steane-code implementation with partially fault-tolerant analog $R_Z(\theta)$ rotations and a Golay-code implementation with higher-order zero-level distillation for fault-tolerant $T$-state preparation. At a physical error rate of $10^{-4}$, our estimates give a megaquop-scale equivalent $T$-count of $1.89\times10^{6}$ for the Steane implementation and a gigaquop-scale characteristic $T$-count of $1.87\times10^{9}$ for the Golay implementation. With sufficient parallel resource supply, MB-FTQC achieves a short online critical path, while resource estimates including verification failures and retries show competitive spacetime costs. These results show that compact, fixed-distance codes can support fault-tolerant computation at substantial scales in the early-FTQC regime, without code concatenation.
item.dc:creator: Yohei Ibe, Yutaka Hirano, Yasuo Ozu, Toru Kawakubo, Keisuke Fujii

item.title: Optimal phase estimation in the presence of correlated dephasing
item.description: arXiv:2511.07211v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate optimal metrological protocols for phase estimation in the presence of correlated dephasing noise, including spin-squeezed state sensing strategies as well as parallel and adaptive protocols optimized using tensor-network-based numerical methods. The results are benchmarked against fundamental bounds obtained either via the latest quantum comb extension method or an optimized classical simulation method. We find that the spin-squeezed states offer practically optimal performance in the regime where phase fluctuations are positively correlated but can be outperformed by tensor-network-optimized strategies for negatively correlated fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Srijon Ghosh, Arkadiusz Kobus, Stanis{\l}aw Kurdzia{\l}ek, Rafa{\l} Demkowicz-Dobrza\'nski

item.title: Quantum Orthogonal Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2511.12613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Quantum Orthogonal Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks (QO-SPINNs), which replace selected dense hidden transformations in physics-informed PDE models with quantum-compatible orthogonal maps. A pyramidal reconfigurable-beamsplitter circuit realizes these maps with $\Theta(d)$ circuit depth. Under the stated signed-readout access model and fixed per-call failure probability, a width-$d$ map has sequential access-cost upper bound $\mathcal O(d\log d/\epsilon^2)$, which is asymptotically smaller than the $\Theta(d^2)$ cost of conventional direct dense multiplication when $\epsilon(d)^{-2}\log d=o(d)$. Because unary state preparation discards magnitude, we retain each hidden-state norm classically and restore it after readout, yielding the exact map $Wh$ under ideal readout. We study this construction in two complementary settings: forward PDE regression and a norm-controlled residual model for representation geometry and uncertainty quantification. In the norm-controlled model, structural orthogonality yields explicit bi-Lipschitz bounds, while finite-readout analysis relates sufficient reconstruction precision to a prescribed physical-coordinate resolution through trained-model constants. This makes the access-cost condition assessable for trained checkpoints, although favorable fixed-resolution scaling across widths is not established. A post-hoc Bayesian-linear covariance provides uncertainty from the same frozen predictor, and cross-PDE transfer shows that strong distance-awareness can persist even when absolute coverage calibration fails. All Quantum Orthogonal (QO) layers are evaluated by classical simulation: the results therefore characterize a quantum-compatible structured neural primitive rather than demonstrating a practical quantum-hardware advantage.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Zanotta, Ljubomir Budinski, Caglar Aytekin, Valtteri Lahtinen

item.title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gate Compilation for Non-semisimple Ising Anyons via Genetic Algorithm-Optimized Solovay-Kitaev Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2511.13194v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-semisimple Ising anyons extend the fusion space of conventional Ising models and offer a new route toward universal topological quantum computation (TQC). However, how to construct a high-fidelity universal quantum gate set that meets fault-tolerant thresholds via braiding operations of non-semisimple Ising anyons remains unexplored. By employing a Genetic Algorithm-enhanced Solovay--Kitaev Algorithm (GA-enhanced SKA), we achieve high-fidelity approximations of standard single-qubit gates (Hadamard $H$-gate and phase $T$-gate) with a recursion level of just three, meeting the fidelity requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Our numerical results demonstrate that for the critical parameter range $\alpha \in [2.001,\, 2.022]$, a few braiding operations can approximate the local equivalence class $[\mathrm{CNOT}]$ with high precision. In contrast to prior theoretical works that established the universality of non-semisimple Ising anyons, this work provides the first complete, executable, and parameter-optimized compilation scheme for high-fidelity universal gates. It quantifies the relationship between the key physical parameter $\alpha$ and gate fidelity, and it delivers direct numerical evidence for the universality of non-semisimple Ising anyons.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwei Long, Zihui Liu, Yizhi Li, Jianxin Zhong, Lijun Meng

item.title: Some Mechanisms for the Quantum Mpemba Effect
item.description: arXiv:2512.13509v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In recent years, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME) which occurs when an out-of-equilibrium system reaches equilibrium faster than another that is closer to equilibrium has attracted significant attention from the scientific community as an intriguing and counterintuitive phenomenon. It generalizes its classical counterpart, extending the concept beyond thermal equilibration. This paper approaches the QME for Markovian open quantum systems from different perspectives. Firstly, we propose a physical mechanism based on decoherence-free subspaces. Secondly, we show that a macroscopic enhancement of the decay rate that scales linearly with system size can be obtained, leading to an extreme version of the phenomenon on Markovian open quantum systems. Thirdly, we study the Mpemba effect through the unravelings of Davies maps, revealing subtleties in the figures of merit which are chosen for obtaining the QME. Lastly, we propose a microscopic model for a better understanding of thermal bath dynamics in this context.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo F. Saliba, Vitor M. Pereira, Raphael C. Drumond

item.title: Hybrid Quantum Repeater Chains with Atom-based Quantum Processing Units and Quantum Memory Multiplexers
item.description: arXiv:2512.21655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum repeaters enable the generation of reliable entanglement across long distances despite the underlying channel noise. Nevertheless, realizing quantum repeaters poses a difficult engineering challenge due to various device constraints and design tradeoffs. Herein we propose and analyze an efficient hybrid quantum repeater design that integrates atom-based quantum processing units, spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources, and atomic frequency comb quantum memories. Our design leverages the strong spectrotemporal multiplexing capability of the quantum memory to enable high-rate elementary-link entanglement generation between repeater nodes. Transferring the photonic entanglement into matter-qubit entanglement, together with deterministic quantum operations, further enables reliable long-distance entanglement distribution. We analyze photon-loss channels in the hybrid architecture and propose suitable error-suppression strategies that are natively incorporated into our repeater protocol. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate the advantages of our hybrid design for end-to-end secret key rates in a linear repeater-chain model. With continued advances in relevant hardware technologies, we envision that the proposed hybrid design is well suited for large-scale quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Shin Sun, Daniel Bhatti, Shaobo Gao, David Elkouss, Hiroki Takahashi

item.title: Gauge-Invariant Phase Mapping to Intensity Lobes of Structured Light via Closed-Loop Atomic Dark States
item.description: arXiv:2512.23642v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an analytical model showing how the gauge-invariant loop phase in a three-level closed-loop atomic system imprints as bright-dark lobes in Laguerre Gaussian probe beam intensity patterns. In the weak probe limit, the output intensity in such systems include Beer-Lambert absorption, a scattering term and loop phase dependent interference term with optical depth controlling visibility. These systems enable mapping of arbitrary phases via interference rotation and offer a platform to measure Berry phase. Berry phase emerge as a geometric holonomy acquired by the dark states during adiabatic traversal of LG phase defined in a toroidal parameter space. Manifesting as fringe shifts which are absent in open systems, experimental realization using cold atoms or solid state platforms appears feasible, positioning structured light in closed-loop systems as ideal testbeds for geometric phases in quantum optics.
item.dc:creator: Nayan Sharma, Ajay Tripathi

item.title: Ising Blockade of Resonant Transport in Dense Spin Ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2602.04721v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV), substitutional-nitrogen (P1), and surface spins in diamond are leading platforms for quantum sensing, masers, and many-body physics, and in all of them polarization moves by resonant flip-flops (pairwise spin exchanges). We show that the Ising part of the dipolar Hamiltonian, which moves no polarization, sets how fast polarization moves. It detunes every flip-flop by exactly the difference of the Ising fields that the other spins exert on the pair, and these fields come from the very couplings that drive hopping. Dipolar transport thus throttles its own rate, an effect we call the Ising blockade, which models have so far absorbed into a measured or fitted disorder width. Deep in the blockade and at fixed composition, the diffusion constant scales as $D \propto J_0\rho^{1/3}$ (coupling $J_0$, density $\rho$) instead of the F\"orster-type $J_0^2\rho^{4/3}$. Without fitting, the theory predicts the NV linewidth and all five P1 diffusion constants of [Nature 597, 45 (2021)] within $2\sigma$; without the Ising term at the same couplings, it overshoots them five- to fifteenfold. On a spin-locked surface [Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 050801 (2025)], the same blockade acts coherently: in exact dynamics, over a third of the spins stay polarized far longer than flip-flops alone allow, accounting for the measured four- to ninefold slowdown.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Ze Ding, Jiu-Qing Liang

item.title: Entropy Bounds via Hypothesis Testing and Its Applications to Two-Way Key Distillation in Quantum Cryptography
item.description: arXiv:2602.05870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) achieves information-theoretic security for a shared secret key, using distributed quantum states. To establish secret bits, two honest parties apply key distillation protocols to the resulting measurement outcomes. In this work, we establish a rigorous connection between the key rate achievable by applying two-way key distillation, such as advantage distillation, and quantum hypothesis testing, via an integral representation of the conditional entropy in terms of the error probabilities of binary state discrimination. This connection significantly improves bounds on key rates at finite blocklengths relative to existing fidelity-based bounds. Moreover, in an important special case, it closes the gap between the known sufficient and conjectured necessary conditions for key generation in the large-blocklength limit. More generally, it establishes a matching asymptotic necessary condition, leaving the corresponding finite-blocklength result open. More broadly, our work shows how results in quantum hypothesis testing can directly sharpen the security analysis of QKD.
item.dc:creator: Rutvij Bhavsar, Junguk Moon, Joonwoo Bae

item.title: Operational performance of finite-key entanglement-based satellite quantum key distribution
item.description: arXiv:2602.11833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Establishing information-theoretically secure communication between arbitrary locations on Earth is a central goal of quantum networking, for which space-based distribution of quantum entanglement is a leading approach. Modelling and analysis of the performance of satellite entanglement pair distribution is therefore important for the architecture and design of future constellations and space systems. However, entanglement-based quantum key distribution in the absence of quantum repeaters, is especially prone to finite-key effects due to low coincident count rates compared to trusted-node single-path links. Quantifying these effects under realistic orbital conditions is therefore essential for the design of practical satellite quantum communication systems. Here, we develop a high-fidelity model of pair distribution from a low-Earth-orbit satellite that captures orbital dynamics, elevation-dependent loss, background noise, and extraneous detector effects. Integrating this with a finite-key security framework for the BBM92 protocol, we optimise the secret key length across different overpass geometries, orbital altitudes, and optical ground station (OGS) separations. We show that secure key generation remains feasible in early clear daytime conditions using baseline parameters representative of current technologies, while showing that modest system improvements could further extend daytime operation. Finally, we evaluate the annual secret key performance for representative intercity-scale OGS pairings. Our results provide quantitative performance bounds and practical design guidelines for near-term entanglement-based satellite QKD, enabling informed trade-offs between satellite payload complexity, ground infrastructure, and achievable secure key throughput.
item.dc:creator: Jasminder S. Sidhu, Sarah E. McCarthy, Cameron Paterson, Nathan Walk, Jens Eisert, Daniel K. L. Oi

item.title: Trainable, self-verifying variational quantum eigensolver using adiabatic warm starts
item.description: arXiv:2602.17612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an adiabatic variant of the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) in which VQE is performed iteratively for a sequence of Hamiltonians along an adiabatic path. We derive the conditions under which gradient-based optimization successfully prepares the adiabatic ground states. These conditions define a trainable tracking region. Additionally, when combined with a gap lower bound, energy-standard-deviation measurements certify eigenstate accuracy at run-time and verify convergence to the global optimum.
item.dc:creator: Bojan \v{Z}unkovi\v{c}, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, Michael Lubasch

item.title: Multipartite Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality from interwoven frustrated down-conversion
item.description: arXiv:2602.18381v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a theory of an interference process that starts with $N$ coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion (PDC) sources, whose output modes are directed to $N$ observers such that each observer receives modes from two different source crystals. Each observation station is equipped with a locally controlled PDC crystal, coherently pumped with the source crystals, whose output modes are perfectly aligned with the input modes from the source PDCs. By varying the local phases of the input modes, perfect $2N$-photon interference can be observed in $2N$ single-photon registrations, one in each output mode of these $N$ local PDCs. The interference results from the indistinguishability of the origins of the detected $2N$ photons: either they all originate from the source PDCs or from the local PDCs. Bell-GHZ nonclassicality of the process emerges when one also considers situations in which at least one of the local PDC processes is blocked. In such cases, the $2N$-photon interference disappears. A ''lifted`` Clauser-Horne inequality is violated when its sole negative term, involving all observers with all local pumps active, is tuned to maximal destructive interference, while all other terms involve settings in which one of the local pumps is off.
item.dc:creator: Marek \.Zukowski, Pawe{\l} Cie\'sli\'nski, Marcin Markiewicz, Konrad Schlichtholz

item.title: Partial Reversibility and Counterdiabatic Driving in Nearly Integrable Systems
item.description: arXiv:2602.22317v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adiabatic (or reversible) processes are the key concept unifying our understanding of thermodynamics and dynamical systems. Reversibility in the thermodynamic sense is understood as entropy-preserving processes, such as in the idealized Carnot engine, whereas in integrable dynamical systems it is understood as the conservation of the action variables. Between these two idealized limits, however, things are much less clear. In this work, we study several toy models to assess the extent to which reversible processes are even possible in this regime. We then explore how the dissipative losses resulting from rapidly driving these kinds of systems can be fought by approximate counterdiabatic driving. Finally, we provide numerical evidence that much of the phenomenology should be the same for quantum many-body systems with large degeneracy in the presence of integrability breaking perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Rohan Banerjee, Shahyad Khamnei, Anatoli Polkovnikov, Stewart Morawetz

item.title: Extreme Quantum Cognition Machines for Deliberative Decision Making
item.description: arXiv:2603.05430v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Extreme Quantum Cognition Machines, a class of quantum learning architectures for deliberative decision making designed to operate under coarse-grained, ambiguous, and potentially contradictory information. Inspired by the quantum cognition paradigm, Extreme Quantum Cognition Machines are closely related to quantum extreme learning and quantum reservoir computing, where fixed quantum dynamics generates a nonlinear feature map and learning is confined to a linear readout. A dynamical attention mechanism, implemented through an input-dependent interaction term in the Hamiltonian, modulates the quantum evolution and biases the resulting feature embedding toward task-relevant correlations. The approach is validated on linguistic classification tasks, which serve as paradigmatic examples of deliberative inference. Hardware-compatible quantum implementations of the proposed framework are discussed, together with potential applications in symbolic inference, sequence analysis, anomaly detection, and automatic diagnosis, with direct relevance to domains such as biology, forensics, and cybersecurity.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Romeo, Jacopo Settino

item.title: Universal purification dynamics in real non-unitary quantum processes
item.description: arXiv:2603.10751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study purification dynamics in monitored quantum processes governed by ensembles of quantum circuits in different random-matrix symmetry classes. We analyze the universal aspects that emerge away from the measurement induced phase transition and inside the volume/weak measurement phase and in the scaling limit of large time and Hilbert space dimension. We present two toy models that reveal two complementary visions and provide quantitative access to universal scaling: i) a discrete-time dynamic in which each time step corresponds to multiplication by a Gaussian random matrix; ii) weak continuous-time monitoring that induces a Dyson brownian motion of the eigenvalues of the density matrix. The first approach provides an algebraic characterization based on rotational invariance emerging in Kraus's operator space, focusing in particular on the unitary and orthogonal cases, respectively $\beta=2$ and $\beta=1$, with $\beta$ the Dyson random-matrix index. The second approach, on the other hand, allows for a unified treatment for any $\beta$, thanks to the mapping of the Fokker-Planck evolution of eigenvalues onto the Calogero-Sutherland integrable Hamiltonian diagonalized in terms of Jack polynomials. We provide explicit expressions for the universal decrease of R\'enyi entropies. We show that, approaching the universal scaling limit, numerical simulations of different models agree with each other and with our theoretical predictions. Our results clarify the existence of different classes of universality for the purification process in hybrid quantum systems, accessible in random circuit architectures and weak measurement protocols.
item.dc:creator: Federico Gerbino, Donghoon Kim, Guido Giachetti, Andrea De Luca, Xhek Turkeshi

item.title: Logarithmic-depth quantum state preparation of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2603.16527v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum state preparation is a central primitive in many quantum algorithms, yet it is generally resource intensive, with efficient constructions known only for structured families of states. This work introduces a method for preparing quantum states whose amplitudes are given by a degree$-d$ polynomial, using circuits with logarithmic depth in the number $n$ of qubits and only $\mathcal O(n)$ ancilla qubits, improving previous approaches that required linear-depth circuits. The construction first relies on a block-encoding of an affine diagonal operator based on its Pauli-basis decomposition, which involves only $n$ terms. A modified linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) technique is introduced to implement this decomposition in logarithmic depth, together with a novel circuit for the EXACT-one oracle that flags basis states in which exactly one qubit is in the state $|1\rangle$. It then uses a generalized quantum eigenvalue transformation (GQET) to promote this affine operator to an arbitrary degree polynomial. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations are reported along with a proof-of-principle implementation on a trapped-ion quantum processor using $14$ qubits and more than $500$ primitive quantum gates. Because polynomial approximations are ubiquitous in scientific computing, this construction provides a scalable and resource-efficient approach to quantum state preparation, further improving the potential of quantum algorithms in fields such as chemistry, physics, engineering, and finance.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Claudon, Alexis Lucas, Jean-Philip Piquemal, C\'esar Feniou, Julien Zylberman

item.title: Latent Style-based Quantum Wasserstein GAN for Drug Design
item.description: arXiv:2603.22399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The development of new drugs is a time-consuming and expensive process, with average costs estimated to be up to around $2.5 billion. The first step in this process is the design of the new drug, for which de novo drug design, assisted by artificial intelligence, has blossomed in recent years and has revolutionized the field. In particular, generative artificial intelligence has delivered promising results in drug discovery and development, reducing costs and time to solution. However, classical generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), can be difficult to train and are prone to mode collapse. Quantum computing may be an avenue to overcome some of these issues, providing compact models with far fewer trainable parameters, thereby enhancing the generalizability of GANs. We propose a new latent style-based quantum Wasserstein GAN (QGAN) for drug design, combining a variational autoencoder that maps molecular structures into a latent space with a hybrid quantum GAN. Our pipeline is benchmarked against classical models of the industry-relevant MOSES suite. Style-based noise reuploading at every rotational gate and a Wasserstein gradient penalty are used to improve trainability and to mitigate mode collapse. Training and large-scale sampling with circuits of up to 15 qubits are performed on noiseless quantum simulators to validate our architecture. We present an inference-only demonstration on an IBM Heron quantum computer using 5 qubits, sampling 2,500 new molecules, to investigate quantum noise effects. Our default QGAN, using 110 trainable generator parameters, reaches statistically comparable overall performance and statistically significant gains on selected drug-relevant metrics relative to both the MOSES classical latent GAN baseline, which contains about 700,000 trainable parameters for the generator, and a classical latent GAN with matched generator capacity.
item.dc:creator: Julien Baglio, Yacine Haddad, Richard Polifka

item.title: Learning unified control of intrinsic nonlinear spin dynamics in atomic qudits for magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2603.28421v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generating and preserving metrologically useful quantum states is a central challenge in quantum-enhanced metrology. In low-field atomic magnetometry with multilevel atoms, the nonlinear Zeeman (NLZ) effect is both a resource and a limitation. It can generate internal spin squeezing within a single atomic qudit, but under fixed readout it also rotates and distorts the measurement-relevant quadrature, limiting the usable metrological gain. The problem is further complicated by the time dependence of both the squeezing axis and the nonlinear evolution itself. Here we show that reinforcement learning can transform NLZ dynamics from a source of readout degradation into a sustained metrological resource. Using only experimentally accessible low-order spin moments, a trained agent identifies a unified control policy for this class of intrinsically nonlinear sensing dynamics. We illustrate the approach in the \(f=21/2\) manifold of \(^{161}\mathrm{Dy}\), where the learned policy rapidly prepares strongly squeezed internal states and stabilizes more than \(4\,\mathrm{dB}\) of fixed-axis spin squeezing under continuous NLZ evolution. Including state-preparation overhead, the learned protocol yields a single-atom magnetic-field sensitivity of \(13.9\,\mathrm{pT}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}\), approximately \(3\,\mathrm{dB}\) beyond the standard quantum limit. Our results establish learning-based control as an experimentally feasible route for converting unavoidable intrinsic nonlinear dynamics in multilevel atomic sensors into operational metrological advantage.
item.dc:creator: C. Z. Cao, J. Z. Han, M. Xiong, M. Deng, L. Wang, Q. Liu, X. Lv, M. Xue

item.title: Bounding the entanglement of a state from its spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2604.02420v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a framework to upper bound the entanglement content of a bipartite quantum state from its spectrum alone. Using linear maps and their inverses, we derive rigorous constraints on the maximal entanglement that can be activated under global unitary transformations. We use as entanglement quantifiers the negativity and the Schmidt number; however, our framework is general and applies to any other entanglement measure. Our approach yields compact analytical sufficient criteria for bounding the entanglement of full-rank states in arbitrary dimensions and reveals new spectral constraints on Schmidt number witnesses.
item.dc:creator: Jofre Abellanet-Vidal, Guillem M\"uller-Rigat, Albert Rico, Anna Sanpera

item.title: Decoherence-Induced Multiphoton Interference
item.description: arXiv:2604.05422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Decoherence is usually deemed detrimental to quantum information processing. Its control and minimization require significant costs and operating overheads, constituting a major hurdle to the practical deployment of quantum technologies. Yet, quantum mechanics provides for counterintuitive, sometimes surprisingly useful, phenomena and effects associated with decoherence, leading to unusual practical utilities. Here we demonstrate such an example of fundamental interest and practical potential, where quantum interference is created among multiple photons through their dissipative coupling to a shared reservoir. On a thin-film lithium niobate chip, we dissipatively link two spontaneous parametric down-converters through a common, highly lossy channel to create phase-sensitive multiphoton states. Our results show that faithful correlations can be established among two, three, and four photons, and tuned by shifting the relative phase between the driving pumps for the converters. This experiment highlights an under-explored territory in quantum science and technology, where loss and decoherence serve as resources, rather than adversaries, for quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Du, Jiuyi Zhang, Daniel L\'opez Mart\'inez, Santosh Kumar, Misagh Izadi, Yuping Huang

item.title: Optimization of entanglement harvesting with arbitrary temporal profiles: the limit of second order perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2604.06303v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the protocol of entanglement harvesting when two local probes couple to the vacuum of a real scalar quantum field with arbitrary temporal profiles. We use a Hermite expansion to efficiently compute smeared field propagators in closed-form, recasting the negativity between the probes as a matrix product. We then optimize the protocol under different signalling conditions, enhancing entanglement harvesting by several orders of magnitude. This optimization would take current experimental proposals beyond the regime of second order perturbation theory.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Morote-Balboa, T. Rick Perche

item.title: Single-Satellite Quantum Repeater Performance Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2604.16165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Satellite optical links may be able to extend quantum communication range beyond that which is possible through optical fibres which are constrained by exponential loss scaling. Quantum repeaters have been proposed to mitigate high channel losses in both fibre and satellite links. Although satellite quantum repeaters could improve entanglement distribution efficiency, the attempt rate is constrained by classical communication latency in the entanglement swapping step. Direct entanglement distribution does not suffer this latency and can therefore compensate for high dual-downlink losses by increasing the source rate. A systematic comparative analysis of repeater-assisted and direct entanglement distribution rates using a satellite is absent from the literature. In addition to entanglement distribution rates, a detailed analysis of the fidelity of entanglement distributed by repeater-assisted satellite links has yet to be performed. Here, we develop an in-depth framework for describing a space quantum link consisting of a single satellite and two ground stations. We compare the entanglement distribution rates of direct and repeater-assisted satellite entanglement distribution, taking into account variations in overpass geometry and quantum memory capacity. The long-term entanglement distribution performance to different pairs of major cities is also considered, and the altitudinal dependence is explored. Furthermore, we develop a Monte Carlo model of the repeater satellite to explore the effect that different memory management policies and capacities have on the waiting time statistics of memory qubits. From these statistics we calculate the fidelity distributions of the entangled pairs established between the ground stations. These results will inform mission design for future space-borne quantum repeater nodes, as well as requirements on space-based memory platforms.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Paterson, Jasminder S. Sidhu, Thomas Brougham, Sarah E. McCarthy, Daniel K. L. Oi

item.title: Algorithmic Locality of Quantum Tensor Network Belief Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2604.21919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Belief propagation has recently emerged as a powerful framework for evaluating tensor networks in higher dimensions, combining computational efficiency with provable analytical guarantees. In this work, we develop the first end-to-end theory of tensor network belief propagation for a class of projected entangled pair states satisfying \emph{strong injectivity}. We show that when the injectivity parameter exceeds a constant threshold, BP fixed points can be found efficiently, and a cluster-corrected BP algorithm computes physical quantities to $1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ error in $\mathrm{poly}(N)$ time for an $N$ qubit system. We further identify a striking phenomenon we term \emph{algorithmic locality}: local perturbations of the tensor network affect the BP fixed point with an influence decaying rapidly with distance. Moreover, through the cluster expansion, this locality extends to observables, implying that local expectation values can be approximated from local data with controlled accuracy. We exhibit three regimes admitting strong injectivity: random Gaussian PEPS with large physical dimension, high-temperature Gibbs states of commuting two-body Hamiltonians, and fixed-depth quantum circuits subject to sufficiently strong depolarizing noise. Our bounds are worst-case sufficient conditions and do not identify sharp algorithmic transitions.
item.dc:creator: Siddhant Midha, Yifan F. Zhang, Daniel Malz, Dmitry A. Abanin, Sarang Gopalakrishnan

item.title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2605.04139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the decay of general initial states out of a metastable potential well in quantum mechanics. We provide a closed-form expression for the probability current that tunnels through the barrier in terms of the resonant states into which the initial state can be decomposed. All ingredients are computed analytically to first subleading order in the semiclassical limit. Specializing to a coherently-oscillating state, we derive an equivalent semiclassical approximation to the current via the path integral, which circumvents the decomposition into resonant states. We test the accuracy of the approximation by comparing it to a numerical solution of the Schr\"odinger equation.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Janssen, Matthew Kleban, Cameron Norton

item.title: Classical shadows over symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.05518v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficiently learning expectation values of unknown quantum states via classical shadows has become an important primitive in both theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum computation. Typically, classical shadow protocols involve randomised measurements induced by sampling uniformly randomly from a compact group, a situation which is now quite well understood. In this work we go beyond this standard assumption, studying the classical shadow protocols occasioned by sampling uniformly randomly from the so-called compact symmetric spaces. We uncover a unifying theory of such protocols, extending the extent to which the general theory of classical shadows is understood at a mathematical level. Interestingly, for the estimation of observables sampled from certain distributions we further find that some of these protocols allow for slight improvements in sample-complexity over existing shadow schemes. As part of our technical analysis we obtain $\varepsilon$-approximate relative-error $k$-designs over the $n$-qubit symplectic group in depth $\mathcal{O}(nk+\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which is optimal with respect to $n$, and may be of some independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Chang, Maureen Krumt\"unger, Martin Larocca, Maxwell West

item.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Building Quantum Circuits for Sets of Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2605.06633v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning nowadays becomes a useful instrument in many subjects. In this paper we use interpretable machine learning to build quantum algorithm. By studying the parameters of the machine learning algorithm we were able to construct universal shortest analytic quantum algorithm for arbitrary diagonal matrix of any size.
item.dc:creator: Matvei Fedin, Andrey Morozov

item.title: Hybrid Qubit-Qutrit Quantum Battery: Nonclassicality and Energy Performance
item.description: arXiv:2605.07449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose and analyze a hybrid qubit-qutrit quantum battery (QB) based on a mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 system interacting via an anisotropic Heisenberg exchange coupling in the presence of a homogeneous magnetic field. The nonclassical properties of the system are characterized using the l1-norm of coherence and negativity, which quantify quantum coherence and entanglement, respectively. The performance of the quantum battery is evaluated through key indicators such as ergotropy, power, and capacity. Our results reveal that both ergotropy and power exhibit oscillatory dynamics, while the capacity remains constant over time. We further investigate the influence of system parameters and magnetic field strength on both quantum correlations and battery performance, demonstrating that nonclassicality plays a crucial role in enhancing energy-storage efficiency. Importantly, we establish a connection between the theoretical model and an experimentally realizable nickel-radical molecular complex, showing that quantum coherence, entanglement, and efficient energy storage persist even at room temperature. These findings provide a realistic pathway toward the implementation of hybrid qubit-qutrit quantum batteries in solid-state molecular platforms.
item.dc:creator: G. Sharvan Prakash, R. Muthuganesan

item.title: Leggett--Garg Tests of Collective Excitation--Inhibition Dynamics in Neuronal Circuits
