item.description: arXiv:2605.12126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent efforts to identify quantum-like signatures in brain and cognition have explored Bell-type tests, temporal inequalities, and Schr\"odinger-inspired models. We propose a Leggett--Garg (LG) test of collective neuronal excitation--inhibition (E--I) dynamics. Two reference configurations, $\ket{E}$ and $\ket{I}$, span an effective two-state space governed by $H_S=\heff\Omega\sigma_x/2$. Spatial separation of the E and I complexes need not preclude coherent superposition: when they constitute distinct subsystems, the corresponding collective alternatives can form an entangled state. The proposal tests temporal correlations, not Bell nonlocality. Complementary feedforward detectors couple selectively to E or I, with ideal negative results enabling non-invasive inference of the opposite configuration. We give a four-output-cell realization of the required projectors and detector interactions. Ideal sequential measurements yield $K_3(\tau)=2\cos(\Omega\tau)-\cos(2\Omega\tau)$, reaching $3/2$. We also derive the four-time result $K_4^{\max}=2\sqrt{2}$ and explain its structural CHSH correspondence through Choi--Jamio{\l}kowski duality. Detector efficiency, false positives, imperfect null results, timing uncertainty, and measurement disturbance are incorporated into a realistic extension. We conclude by identifying the experimental challenges of preparing, controlling, and selectively measuring collective E--I states in neuronal circuits.
item.dc:creator: Partha Ghose

item.title: Terrestrial campaign towards space-to-ground quantum communications with a space-qualified entangled photon-pair system
item.description: arXiv:2605.19689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Realizing a global quantum internet relies on the deployment of robust satellite-based entanglement distribution links. While pioneering demonstrations have established the feasibility of such links, the transition to operational infrastructure demands the validation of robust, integrated space-to-ground architectures. Here, we report on a free-space Quantum Key Distribution experiment conducted over a 1.8 km free-space link using an engineering model of the quantum payload onboard the SpeQtre satellite and the Abu Dhabi Quantum Optical Ground Station. By implementing a BBM92 protocol with polarization-entangled photons, a mean secret key rate of 7.57 kbps with a mean quantum bit error rate of 4.78%+-0.24% was produced. The deployed system featured spectral and spatial filtering approaches identical to those in the space segment, demonstrating their operation in a terrestrial nighttime free-space channel. These results confirm the operational compatibility between the ground and space segments, establishing a critical performance baseline for the SpeQtre mission and future space-based, large-scale quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca De Santis, Jia Boon Chin, Srihari Sivasankaran, Konstantin Kravtsov, Chin Chean Lim, Aitor Villar, Robert Bedington, Sana Amairi-Pyka, Eleni Diamanti, Alexander Ling, James A. Grieve

item.title: Stronger Entanglement Dies Faster: Quantum Mpemba Effect in Dissipative Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2605.23197v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In classical thermodynamics, the Mpemba effect refers to the counterintuitive observation that hot water can freeze faster than cold water, manifesting as an anomalous crossing of dynamical trajectories. While analogues of this phenomenon have been explored in open quantum systems and spin-chain entanglement asymmetry, its connection to the finite-time loss of entanglement remains elusive. In this work, we report a distinct Mpemba effect for quantum entanglement in a dissipative quantum system associated with entanglement sudden death (ESD). By analyzing two qubits interacting with local amplitude damping reservoirs, we demonstrate that a more strongly entangled initial state can experience a faster collapse into a separable state than a more weakly entangled state. This anomalous decay stems from the competition between initial coherence and excited-state population, where the latter acts as a catalyst for ESD. We provide exact analytical derivations for the trajectory crossover and ESD time, and map the phase diagram to precisely identify the parameter regime where the effect occurs. Our results offer a new strategy for controlling the lifetime of quantum resources in dissipative environments.
item.dc:creator: Zhilong Liu, Zehua Tian, Jieci Wang

item.title: The bulk spectral gap is certifiable from above but uncomputable from below
item.description: arXiv:2606.03836v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Determining spectral gaps in the thermodynamic limit is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. When a fixed boundary condition is imposed, this problem is undecidable: no algorithm, even with unlimited resources, can decide for every Hamiltonian whether it is gapped. Yet the thermodynamic limit is meant to capture the intrinsic properties of very large systems, which should not depend on how their boundaries are chosen. We therefore consider the bulk spectral gap, which concerns only the intrinsic excitations of the infinite system, and ask what can and cannot be computed about it. First, we give a general algorithm producing a hierarchy of certified upper bounds on the bulk gap, arbitrarily tight at the cost of more computation. Second, we prove that the spectral gap problem remains undecidable in the bulk, already for translationally invariant nearest-neighbour chains of fixed local dimension. Hence no general algorithm produces convergent lower bounds, and no convergent upper-bounding algorithm, ours included, admits a computable convergence rate. The bulk spectral gap is thus certifiable from above but uncomputable from below; more precisely, the bulk-gaplessness promise problem is RE-complete, exactly as hard as the halting problem. The same construction shows that no general algorithm can decide whether a given product state is a ground state, and that convergent bounds on ground-state expectation values admit no computable convergence rate in general. Finally, we obtain the first nontrivial certified upper bounds on the bulk gap of the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.
item.dc:creator: Xiangling Xu, Matthias Sch\"otz, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Igor Klep, Omar Fawzi, Marc-Olivier Renou

item.title: Grid-state deformation in a no-jump non-Hermitian bosonic dimer
item.description: arXiv:2606.17036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the no-jump evolution of ideal grid states in a lossy bosonic dimer with differential decay. The effective non-Hermitian quadratic dynamics induces a complex symplectic flow in phase space that deforms both the primitive lattice vectors and the origin seed. The average decay rate controls common-mode attenuation, while coherent hopping and differential decay control the reduced dimer deformation. For resonant modes, the reduced displacement flow is oscillatory in the elliptic regime, linear at the exceptional point, and exponentially separating in the hyperbolic regime. Although projected lattice areas can change, the deformation comes from a determinant-one complex symplectic flow on the complexified phase space. For a Gaussian regularization of the origin seed in the resonant dimer, we derive the associated complex width matrix and show that the seed remains square-integrable and Gaussian for every positive initial width, all non-negative times, and all physical loss rates. For an initial two-mode qunaught product state, the lossless limit recovers the standard beam-splitter generation of a square Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill Bell pair, while the no-jump dynamics produces its non-Hermitian deformation. The full no-jump probability for a normalized finite-energy input sets the postselection cost and depends on its excitation-number distribution and the reduced dimer dynamics.
item.dc:creator: B. M. Rodriguez-Lara, H. Ghaemi-Dizicheh, S. Dehdashti, A. Hanke, A. Touhami, J. N\"otzel

item.title: Connecting Quantum Tomography and Quantum Retrodiction
item.description: arXiv:2606.23777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum tomography and quantum retrodiction are traditionally viewed as separate inference tasks. We show that the two are manifestations of the same underlying principle. We prove that the Petz recovery map of a measurement channel is a gradient of the log-likelihood used in maximum-likelihood tomography, and we derive its extension to arbitrary quantum channels. Consequently, for measurement channels, repeated applications of the Petz map monotonically increase the likelihood, naturally yielding a method for quantum tomography.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Murk, Ian Tan, Fabian M\"uller, Dominik \v{S}afr\'anek

item.title: Scalable Message-Passing Quantum Graph Neural Networks in the Weisfeiler-Leman Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2606.26873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphs provide a natural language for relational data in chemistry, biology and optimisation. Graph neural networks (GNNs) have driven much of the recent progress in learning from such data through message passing, a single primitive that generalises convolution and attention. Quantum counterparts have been proposed, but with limited connection to message passing and few guarantees on performance or scalability. More broadly, the trainability of variational quantum circuits is a recognised bottleneck for their wide applicability, and pre-training has emerged as one way to address it. Yet for a quantum model to be useful, it must offer expressivity guarantees along with demonstrable scalability. Here we show how a quantum graph neural network can be built to perform message passing, to be permutation equivariant, and to sit at a chosen level of the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy, the standard measure of how finely a model can tell graphs apart. We show that, as for classical GNNs, the training can be done first on small graph instances, allowing for a pre-training that can mitigate usual training issues, and its output can be read out at a cost that stays low as the graph grows. We validate the framework in large-scale simulations of up to 56 qubits across three datasets, on synthetic graphs that ordinary message passing cannot separate, on molecular property prediction, and on the travelling salesperson problem. Our framework opens a path for near-term quantum algorithms with theoretical guarantees and practical scalability, bringing the principles of graph learning into quantum circuit design.
item.dc:creator: Snehal Raj, Brian Coyle, L\'eo Monbroussou, Andr\'e J. Ferreira-Martins, Renato M. S. Farias, Elham Kashefi

item.title: Broadband characterization of polarization mode dispersion for quantum communication channels
item.description: arXiv:2607.03202v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a method for characterizing depolarization in fiber channels carrying broadband polarization-encoded optical signals. Wavelength-dependent polarization mode dispersion maps each input polarization to a trajectory on the Poincar\'e sphere; we show that the singular value decomposition of the band-averaged rotation matrix yields, in closed form, the optimal input states, the associated mutually unbiased measurement bases, and the resulting projection error probabilities. The three singular values provide a compact, bandwidth-dependent channel signature that distinguishes first- from higher-order dispersion, and yield the bandwidth at which the worst-case error probability reaches 3% as a practical filtering budget. We perform a second-order analysis of the band average that treats the two higher-order mechanisms: variation of the differential group delay at a fixed principal-state axis and wander of that axis with wavelength. We characterize 12 deployed fiber links in Masdar City and demonstrate mitigation by concatenating two channels through a single polarization controller, a step towards nonlocal compensation. The analysis is implemented in an openly available Python library for fiber-channel characterization.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Rodimin, Konstantin Kravtsov, Rui Ming Chua, Xingjian Zhang, Aleksei Ponasenko, Yury Kurochkin, Alexander Ling, James A. Grieve

item.title: Chromatic Constraints on Quantum Observables: Gaps, Contextuality, and Separability
item.description: arXiv:2607.04289v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intertwined complete projective experiments share outcomes, motivating the search for a common spectral labeling across contexts. Strong coloring tests whether complete contexts admit one context-independent nondegenerate spectrum; when that labeling exists, chromatic separability tests which event distinctions it preserves. We distinguish these questions from ordinary Kochen--Specker statelessness, geometric realizability, event-order representation, and Born-probability models. A state extends to a strong d-coloring exactly when deletion of its support leaves a (d-1)-colorable graph. Faithful real 17- and 21-ray restrictions of completed Yu--Oh have separating ordinary states but forced color identities; one quantum preparation requires exactly 1/9 nonextendable weight despite admitting an ordinary-state model. Independent Hermitian projection arguments correct earlier inferences from a chromatic gap to statelessness or nonrealizability. Hesse's complex 37-ray example separates real and complex geometry and has exact state-family minima 6/7/18 for three representation requirements. A rational two-plane construction gives a linear real 65-ray example with 393,216 states and explicit event-order and probability failures. General and specified ancestry results distinguish geometric KS extensions from abstract chromatic-to-stateless constructions. Detailed enumerations, regenerated state certificates, and extended proofs are supplementary.
item.dc:creator: Karl Svozil

item.title: Depth-Efficient Quantum Topological Data Analysis for Regime-Specific Detection of Financial Stress
item.description: arXiv:2607.09906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present, to our knowledge, the first adaptation of Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) to quantum topological data analysis, reformulating Betti number estimation as a depth-efficient variational optimization over a compressed qubit register. From a Takens embedding and Vietoris-Rips filtration of S&P 500 returns, we extract combinatorial Laplacians and recast null-space counting as a continuous-PCE Rayleigh-quotient minimization with variational deflation, encoding $n_k$ simplex indices into $O(n_k^{1/\kappa})$ qubits with shallow, ancilla-free circuits. Because the resulting loss is rational rather than bilinear in the correlators, the barren-plateau bound of Sciorilli et al. does not transfer; empirically the gradient variance decays only polynomially, with no exponential barren plateau, over $n=4$-$12$ qubits. The classical stage matches ripser on all 190 sliding windows (2003-2010). On the real market Laplacians ($\beta_1=1$-$22$), PCE-VQE recovers no null vector from a random start, but warm-starting from a classical null-space surrogate recovers $\beta_1$ exactly on all seven windows tested ($n_k \le 259$), placing the obstacle in the optimization landscape rather than the encoding. Chronologically split classification gives in-regime ROC AUC 0.818, but out-of-distribution evaluation on the 2020 COVID shock and 2022 rate cycle (AUC 0.009, 0.515) shows the calibration does not generalize across crisis regimes.
item.dc:creator: Arul Rhik Mazumder, Shreyan Ronit Mazumder

item.title: Norm of resonance states in quantum scattering and electromagnetic systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.22052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Resonance states spatially diverge and are thus not square integrable. Instead, their norm is defined by the biorthogonal scalar product of left and right states. We replace the corresponding volume integral over infinite space by a convenient boundary integral in piecewise-homogeneous systems and apply this procedure to diverse physical settings. For a quantum particle in any number of dimensions we treat hard-wall and piecewise-constant potentials. For electromagnetic systems with piecewise-homogeneous material properties, we consider three-dimensional and effectively two-dimensional cavities.
item.dc:creator: Florian Lorenz, Jan M\"oseritz-Schmidt, Roland Ketzmerick

item.title: PhD thesis: Modes, States, and Symmetries in quantum Optics for quantum Information and Metrology
item.description: arXiv:2607.26761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This thesis explores the role of modes, states, and symmetries in quantum optics, within the context of quantum information and quantum metrology. It proposes a unified framework to analyze how the modal structure of photonic fields, the statistical nature of states, and their symmetry properties determine the physical resources that can be exploited for quantum information processing and quantum parameter estimation. A first line of investigation develops a description of time-frequency degrees of freedom as continuous quantum variables, highlighting their richness for encoding and manipulating information. A second axis studies entanglement and collective variables, clarifying the link between physical resources and metrological gains, particularly in reaching ultimate precision limits. Interferometric scenarios of the Hong-Ou-Mandel type are then analyzed, and a general formalism centered on the notion of symmetry is developed. This framework enables the analysis of a broad range of situations and leads to several generalizations. Finally, the thesis examines the symmetries imposed by optical superselection rules and their consequences for the structure of quantum states and their operational performance, with the aim of providing a deeper understanding of the foundations of quantum optics.
item.dc:creator: \'Eloi Descamps

item.title: A Unified Complexity Framework for Quantum Property Testing
item.description: arXiv:2608.02600v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a unified framework for analyzing the complexity of quantum property testing through functionals of the form $\mathcal{L}_{\phi}(\rho) = \operatorname{tr}(\phi(d\rho))/d$, where $\rho$ is an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state and $\phi$ is a given function. A master theorem is established that derives sample complexity lower bounds for estimating $\mathcal{L}_\phi(\rho)$ from properties of $\phi$, combining Haar-random moment encoding with moment matching and best polynomial approximation. Corresponding query complexity lower bounds follow from quantum sample-to-query lifting. The framework yields (nearly) tight bounds for a broad class of problems, including entropy estimation (von Neumann, R\'enyi, and Tsallis), closeness estimation (trace distance and Uhlmann fidelity), spectrum estimation, rank testing (operator rank, Schmidt rank, and matrix product states). In particular, combined with known upper bounds, we show that the sample complexity of von Neumann entropy estimation is \[ \Theta\!\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon\log^2(d)\max\{1, \varepsilon\log^2(d)\}} + \frac{\log^2(d)}{\varepsilon^2}\right), \] and the sample complexity of spectrum estimation is \[ \Theta\!\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\{1, \varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\}}\right). \] In summary, our results resolve several open problems and establish the optimality of 37 quantum algorithms since 2015, up to constant or polylogarithmic factors.
item.dc:creator: Qisheng Wang

item.title: From Barren Plateaus to SPSA Optimization in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
item.description: arXiv:2608.09810v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The barren plateau (BP) phenomenon poses a fundamental challenge to the trainability of variational quantum eigensolvers (VQEs) by causing exponentially vanishing gradients as the system size increases. While extensive studies have investigated the geometric origins of BP, its impact on the optimization dynamics and complexity of practical algorithms under finite-shot measurements has received comparatively less attention. In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework that characterizes how the BP affects the optimization dynamics of the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) algorithm and quantifies the resulting iteration complexity and measurement budget. We derive non-asymptotic bias and variance bounds for the SPSA gradient estimator, introduce a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) defined as the ratio of the gradient energy to the mean squared error of the estimator, and establish convergence guarantees for SPSA under finite-shot measurements. Our results show that, under the proposed parameter schedules, the number of iterations sufficient to guarantee a fixed relative first-order stationarity level scales polynomially with the inverse of the intrinsic gradient energy. Consequently, when this energy decays exponentially under BP, the resulting guaranteed iteration complexity and total measurement budget both grow exponentially with the number of qubits.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Qin

item.title: Superselection Rigidity of Topological Calderbank--Shor--Steane Codes: From Koszul-Complex Models to Nonsplit Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2608.09913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can excitation structure classify topological quantum codes up to finite-depth local circuits? For translation-invariant topological Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes in arbitrary dimensions, we introduce excitation superselection profiles $\mathscr E_\sigma$ ($\sigma=X,Z$). Their cohomology layers $E_\sigma^\ell:=H^\ell(\mathscr E_\sigma)$ encode excitation types, fusion rules, and translation action, while $\mathscr E_\sigma$ retains cross-degree gluing. Pointlike, looplike, and higher-dimensional excitations correspond to degrees $\ell=1,2,\ldots$, respectively. Our matrix-level Schanuel-lemma method proves single-degree superselection rigidity: if $\mathscr E_\sigma$ is supported in a single degree $\ell$, then $E_\sigma^\ell$ and $\ell$ fix the stable translation-invariant Clifford class under a finite-resolution hypothesis automatic for prime qudits. If $E_\sigma^\ell$ is also finite, prime-qudit codes decouple into toric-code stacks by Clifford circuits after coarse graining, with the exact minimal threshold set by the translation kernel. We develop a unified topological theory of Koszul-complex models (encompassing toric codes, bivariate-bicycle codes, and Haah's cubic code): for regular models, we compute $E_\sigma^\ell$, prove $\mathscr E_\sigma$ is single-degree, express finite-torus logical modules as $\mathrm{Tor}$ groups, and obtain coarse-grained toric-stack normal forms at full length. Two constructions extend this framework to realize any admissible single-degree profile and build multi-degree extensions. The latter yields eight 3D qubit toric-code extensions with identical layers in both Pauli sectors and trivial translation action, yet distinct size-dependent ground-state degeneracies. The seven nonsplit models require blocking to decouple. Thus, cross-degree gluing carries translation-symmetry-enriched topological information invisible to individual layers.
item.dc:creator: Hao Song

item.title: Efficient Compilation for Hamiltonian Simulation via Global Binary Symplectic Form Simplification
item.description: arXiv:2608.11579v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hamiltonian simulation is a core quantum workload, underpinning variational quantum algorithms and Trotterized time evolution. Such programs are expressed as Pauli exponential sequences, exhibiting structural patterns that are highly amenable to high-level synthesis and optimization. Existing compilers, however, fail to fully unlock the optimization potential of their global algebraic structure, even when employing advanced graph- or tableau-based methods. We present Symphony, a holistic compilation approach built on the binary symplectic form (BSF) representation of Pauli strings. Unlike prior group-wise BSF simplification and path-based Pauli network synthesis, Symphony applies generalized controlled-Pauli Clifford transformations directly to a global BSF tableau, progressively reducing active Pauli rows while adaptively emitting eligible two-qubit blocks in addition to single-qubit rotations in a forward Clifford frame. Following algebraic simplification, Symphony performs a causality-preserving block rescheduling heuristic that respects frame-induced dependencies while exposing extensive two-qubit block parallelism opportunities. This streamlined compilation style comprehensively exploits simultaneous simplification and commutativity opportunities, achieving efficient global optimization without relying on computationally expensive heuristics or long-horizon searches. Across the generic Hamiltonian simulation benchmarks in HamLib, Symphony achieves average reductions of 59% in two-qubit gate count and 91% in circuit depth. It Pareto-dominates prior state-of-the-art compilers, requiring 1.17--1.58$\times$ fewer two-qubit gates and especially shrinking two-qubit circuit depth by a substantial factor of 1.87--5.67$\times$ on average.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohui Yang, Yuwei Han, Ruiyun Zhang, Dawei Ding, Jianxin Chen, Yuan Feng, Yuan Xie

item.title: Classical Simulation and Design Frontiers for IBM's Doped Clifford Sampling Experiment
item.description: arXiv:2608.13110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classically simulate the IBM doped Clifford random circuit sampling experiment, comprising $70$ qubits, $70$ entangling layers, and $468$ inserted $T$ gates, as reported in the first version of arXiv:2607.25941. A deterministic temporal-boundary tensor network contraction approach is specifically designed to tackle such open-boundary one-dimensional brickwork circuits with operator-Schmidt-rank-$2$ entangling gates. For an $n$-qubit circuit of depth $d$, the resulting unsliced path evaluates an exact amplitude with contraction width $\lceil d/2\rceil$; Ratcatcher calculations certify that no smaller width is possible for the tested instances. Because one-qubit gates are absorbed without changing the network topology, the width and dense scheduled contraction cost are independent of their values and of the number and placement of $T$ gates. For this initial instance, its largest intermediate tensor contains $2^{35}$ complex64 entries (256 times smaller than IBM's estimation), corresponding to a tensor payload of $256$ GiB, and is distributed across eight GPUs within a node. Using 32 nodes, with eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs per node, we completed all 2051 amplitude batches corresponding to IBM's published output bitstrings in 37.3 minutes. The resulting probabilities yield a log-XEB estimate of $0.35034$ with a 95% interval of $[0.29763,0.40305]$. Under the Porter--Thomas and scrambled-noise assumptions, this is numerically compatible with IBM's fidelity lower bound; separately, fidelity-weighted resource accounting projects a 583-contraction workload with a 10.6-minute makespan on the same 32 nodes. More broadly, the approach provides a practical diagnostic for experimental outputs and a quantitative tool for designing future doped Clifford sampling experiments.
item.dc:creator: Hidetaka Manabe, Hanfeng Gu, Feng Pan

item.title: Counterexamples to the Tensorization Property of Strong Data Processing Inequalities for Quantum Divergences
item.description: arXiv:2608.13204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In information theory, the data processing inequality is a fundamental property that describes the loss of information through noisy channels. A more refined description is given by the strong data processing inequality (SDPI) for a fixed channel and a full-rank reference state. In classical information theory, the strong data processing inequality tensorizes for a large family of $f$-divergences. However, its quantum counterpart remains largely unexplored. Tensorization of SDPI has previously been shown only for some special cases, and whether it holds more generally for quantum divergences still remains open. In this work, we report two negative results: the tensorization property fails for certain quantum chi-square divergences, and it also does not hold for the quantum relative entropy.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cao

item.title: Local geometry for Schmidt number witnesses
item.description: arXiv:2608.14199v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose that $F_E$ is the face of the convex set of all $m\otimes n$ bi-partite states which consists of states with ranges contained in a subspace $E$. By the result in [Phys. Rev. A {\bf 112} (2025), 032426], there exist Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses outside of the face $F_{E^\perp}$ if and only if $\ell\le\mu$, where $\mu$ is the minimum of Schmidt ranks of nonzero vectors in $E$. In this paper, we show that every neighborhood of the projection state located at the center of $F_{E^\perp}$ contains Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses if and only if $\ell\ge\mu$. In order to understand the local shape of the convex sets of $k$-blockpositive matrices around this projection state, we introduce principal supporting hyperplanes, and show that they correspond to vectors in $E$ with Schmidt rank $\le k$. Using techniques from algebraic geometry, we show that the inclusions between these convex sets are detected by principal supporting hyperplanes through the projection state for generic subspaces $E$, while for non-generic subspaces they may not be detected by any supporting hyperplane.
item.dc:creator: Young-Hoon Kiem, Seung-Hyeok Kye

item.title: Decay versus dephasing in Rydberg analog optimization: the exchange rate depends on the readout
item.description: arXiv:2608.29858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerical studies of noisy Rydberg-atom optimization compress decoherence into a single rate, treating spontaneous decay ($\Gamma$) and dephasing ($\gamma$) as equivalent. We resolve the two as independent Lindblad axes for quantum annealing of unit-disk maximum independent set at fixed annealing time and ask how their relative effect depends on the readout. For the raw readout the size error collapses onto the effective dephasing rate $u=\kappa\Gamma+\gamma$, and at small noise a unit of decay rate degrades the result as much as $\kappa=7.4$ units of dephasing rate; a collapse fit across the whole grid returns 8.3. After greedy completion followed by a $(1,2)$-swap local search, classical post-processing of polynomial cost, the exchange rate falls to $\kappa=1.6$, and at the calibrated operating point of a commercial device dephasing produces three quarters of the noise-induced error instead of two fifths. First-order perturbation theory built from noiseless propagation gives the decay and dephasing susceptibilities of every readout, raw or post-processed, to a few parts in $10^6$ of the full Lindblad result. The raw asymmetry is set at the end of the schedule, where a decay event deletes an atom and a dephasing event leaves the readout unchanged. Post-processing refills most deletions and leaves misplaced atoms, which the two channels produce at comparable rates. Which channel limits a device therefore depends on the readout as well as on the hardware.
item.dc:creator: Seunghyeon Kim, Minju Kim, Junwoo Jung

item.title: p-Adic Dirac Equations, Continuous-Time Quantum Walks, and Quantum Networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.04358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new class of p-adic Dirac equations, formulated in the standard axiomatic framework of quantum mechanics, in which the ordinary momentum operators are replaced by bounded non-local operators built from arbitrary integrable radial kernels. We diagonalize the free Dirac Hamiltonian in momentum space, construct its plane-wave solutions, and determine its spectrum, which is pure point, with eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity; in the massless case we describe the zero-energy subspace explicitly. We identify the charge-conjugation symmetry of the model: it is given by an antiunitary operator whose square is minus the identity, it exchanges the positive- and negative-energy subspaces, and in an external electromagnetic field it reverses the sign of both the charge and the vector potential. We then discretize the free equation in two ways, both giving genuine continuous-time quantum walks rather than discrete-time, coined walks: one on a countable graph and one on a finite, tree-like graph. In both cases the discretization is exact: the walk is the restriction of the p-adic Dirac evolution to an invariant subspace, and its Hamiltonian is a Dirac-type combination of weighted graph Laplacians with ultrametric weights. We prove that the Born-rule transition probabilities, summed over the internal degrees of freedom and averaged over the initial internal state, form a doubly stochastic matrix at every instant, and that, as for any non-trivial continuous-time quantum walk, this family of matrices is not a Markov semigroup. We discuss how the construction can serve as the foundation of a quantum network with four-component spinor degrees of freedom, complementing earlier, non-relativistic p-adic quantum neural networks, and prove global well-posedness of the associated nonlinear network equation. We close with a discussion of open problems.
item.dc:creator: W. A. Z\'u\~niga-Galindo

item.title: Quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and real matrix-vector query problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.05679v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We (the author and the AI systems that did the heavy lifting) show that the quantum query complexity of minimizing a convex function over a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with evaluation and membership queries is $\tilde\Omega(n)$, nearly matching the best known upper bound. In particular, we show this even for quadratic minimization, which is equivalent to inverting an $n \times n$ real matrix using matrix-vector queries. We also show linear or nearly linear lower bounds on the quantum query complexity of computing the trace, the sign of the determinant, and the magnitude of the determinant of a real matrix in the matrix-vector query model. We use a novel quantum lower bound technique, the determinantal witness method, based on identifying a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and that correlates well with the function being computed.
item.dc:creator: Andrew M. Childs

item.title: Partial Stabilizer Learning under Fixed Commuting Constraints and the Absence of a Copy-Rate Discount
item.description: arXiv:2609.13923v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider an unknown pure stabilizer state of \(n\) qudits with a fixed prime local dimension \(p\), together with prescribed commuting Pauli observables. Rather than learning the whole state, the learner must recover only complementary stabilizers that commute with the prescribed observables, together with their eigenvalues. Once the prescribed measurement is performed, this information and the observed outcome determine the corresponding conditional stabilizer state. We compare the number \(k\) of copies available to the learner with the number \(n\) of qudits and refer to their ratio \(k/n\) as the copy rate. Suppose that the dimension \(m\) of the requested complementary stabilizer subspace satisfies \(m=\beta n+o(n)\) for a fixed \(0<\beta\leq1\). If the copy rate converges to a value below one, the optimal exact recovery probabilities and verification scores converge to zero, both in the worst case and under the uniform prior. Conversely, if the number \(k\) of copies minus the number \(n\) of qudits tends to positive infinity, the entire stabilizer state can be identified with probability tending to one, and the requested complementary information can then be extracted. Thus, restricting the learning target to the stabilizer information needed after the prescribed measurement yields no copy-rate discount.
item.dc:creator: Masahito Hayashi, Yimin Lu

item.title: Non-stabilizerness and entanglement in $(2+1)$-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory using tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.28634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study non-stabilizerness (magic) in the ground state of $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory with matter, formulated in the dressed-site basis in the hardcore-gluon truncation and restricted to the zero baryon-number sector. Using matrix product states, we compute three facets of magic: the second-order stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE) $M_2$, its non-local component $M_2^{\rm NL}$, estimated by the SRE $M_2(\tilde\psi)$ of the computational-basis Schmidt representative $\tilde\psi$, and a lower bound in terms of the anti-flatness $F$ of the entanglement spectrum. We also prove a stronger form of the sandwich relation: $-\log_2(1-4F)\le M_2^{\rm NL}\le M_2$; the lower bound rests on a stronger inequality that we obtain for arbitrary Schmidt bases and rank, with an optimal constant. Combined with recent results, this yields the unconditional bracket $\max\{-\log_2(1-4F),\,M_2(\tilde\psi)-4\}\le M_2^{\rm NL}\le M_2(\tilde\psi)$. We emphasize a structural distinction that makes the non-local quantities the physically preferred diagnostics: whereas the full SRE depends on the (non-unique) encoding of the gauge-invariant local Hilbert space into qubits, the non-local magic, its estimate $M_2(\tilde\psi)$, and the anti-flatness are invariant under site-local re-encodings and are therefore intrinsic to the state and bipartition. By varying the gauge coupling for two values of the fermion mass on lattices up to $8\times 8$ ($\sim 288$ qubits) with bond dimension up to $128$, we find that the non-local magic, as estimated by $M_2(\tilde\psi)$, furnishes a sharper and more bond-dimension-friendly probe of the gauge-matter delocalization crossover compared to the full SRE or the gauge-invariant entanglement entropy, retaining a clear signal at bond dimensions well below those needed to converge the ground state itself.
item.dc:creator: Raghav G. Jha, Jaber I. Taher, Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Goksu C. Toga, Bojko N. Bakalov, Alexander F. Kemper

item.title: Spectral and Impedance Matching for Multi-excitation Charging of an Interacting Quantum Battery via an Anharmonic Mediator
item.description: arXiv:2609.39393v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a finite-time quantum-battery charging architecture in which a driven two-level working system transfers nonequilibrium resources to an interacting two-qubit battery through a weakly anharmonic three-level mediator. Finite-time driving generates coherence and ergotropy, while excitation-number conservation organizes the transfer into distinct dynamical sectors. The mediator then provides spectrally selective charging channels: its lower transition enables nearly complete single-excitation transfer with negligible residual mediator energy, whereas initial mediator loading activates a cross-matched resonant two-excitation cascade toward the doubly excited battery state. In the latter sector, the mediator anharmonicity compensates the interaction-induced non-equidistance of the battery spectrum, enabling simultaneous resonance of the two transfer channels. At exact double resonance, unequal collective matrix elements impose the analytical bound $P_{\rm max}=8/9$; unit transfer is recovered under the impedance-matching condition $|G_1|=|G_2|$, as confirmed numerically. Detuning scans quantify the spectral tolerance, and the full mixed-state dynamics reveals distinct energy- and ergotropy-transfer profiles. Finite-time compression, thermal reset, and switching work close the cycle-level energy balance to numerical precision. The resulting framework combines nonequilibrium resource generation, spectral matching, impedance matching, and coherent multilevel charging, and provides a basis for extending these principles to collective and many-body quantum batteries.
item.dc:creator: Sujay Mondal, Anumita Mukhopadhyay, Siddhartha Dutta, Abhijit Bandyopadhyay

item.title: Harnessing problem structure for end-to-end quantum speed-ups
item.description: arXiv:2609.40105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum algorithms can offer substantial computational speed-ups, yet these advantages may disappear once the cost of structure-agnostic classical data encoding is taken into account. Real-world problem instances, however, often possess rich internal structure. This raises a fundamental question: can such structure be harnessed to make quantum speed-ups survive end-to-end cost accounting? Here we show that it can. We introduce a general framework for structure-aware quantum data encoding that compiles compact recursive descriptions of problem structure into efficient state-preparation circuits, translating structural information directly into reduced encoding complexity. For the uncapacitated facility-location problem, structure-agnostic encoding admits a classical dequantization that eliminates the quadratic quantum speed-up, whereas exploiting the underlying problem structure restores this advantage even when state-preparation costs are included. More broadly, the same framework prepares structured quantum states for combinatorial optimization that capture non-trivial relations among constraints, including group balance, conflicts and synergistic rewards, extending previously reported super-polynomial quantum advantages to broader classes of objectives. These results establish exploitable problem structure as a computational resource for quantum algorithms and provide a systematic route towards realizing quantum advantage in data-intensive problems.
item.dc:creator: Qifan Jiang, Xiao-Ming Zhang, Debin Xiang, Xiao Yuan, Liqiang Lu, Jianwei Yin

item.title: Exact replica-sector hierarchy of multi-resolvent correlations in random free fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.00261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The spectral weight with which a many-body eigenstate contributes to a given channel is not fixed by the smooth one-point ETH envelope, and its higher-order correlations---the connected cumulants of three and more channel-resolved spectral functions---have lacked a systematic organization. We construct one. In random free fermions, where every channel overlap is a squared Slater minor of a Haar-orthogonal one-body eigenvector matrix, the $r$-resolvent moment admits an exact replica-sector decomposition: a sum over the double-coset sectors of the orthogonal Weingarten algebra, in which the permutation sectors are the replica contraction classes and each sector value is determined by the overlap pattern of the channels and of the eigenstates. The sector coefficients follow from an exact occupancy-matrix assembly---a signed convolution over the slot permutations, a decomposition into connected blocks, and a finite-state chain transfer matrix whose local transition rules are independent of $r$ and $k$---so the sector theorem holds at arbitrary finite multiplicity, realized exactly at $r=3$ ($k=2,3,4$), $r=4$ and $r=5$ ($k=2$). The structure carries the physical hierarchy: the fully coincident sector is the projection that yields the Selberg moment ratios $q_r$, the levels are nested by exact marginalization, and the sectors are the multi-energy spectral cumulants behind the resolvent cumulants, with the irreducible self-energy vertices of the Feshbach ladder as the connected kernel. The multi-resolvent correlations of random free fermions are therefore organized, level by level, by one replica-sector algebra---an exact microscopic benchmark for the higher-order fluctuation sector of eigenstate thermalization, with its microscopic sector geometry made explicit.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqiang Huang

item.title: Exact $T$-counts of CCZ layers from an isotropy bound
item.description:
arXiv:2610.01024v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $T$-count is a dominant cost of fault-tolerant Clifford$+T$ computation. We prove that every Hadamard-free Clifford$+T$ circuit with clean ancillas for a layer of $m$ disjoint CCZ gates, the diagonal core of a parallel Toffoli layer, uses at least $6m+1$ $T$ gates. Campbell and Howard gave a circuit with $6m+1$, and to our knowledge this is the first proof that it is optimal for general $m$. The proof combines Campbell and Howard's self-orthogonality of the columns of the parity matrix with a rank (flattening) bound, sharpened by one. More generally, the argument gives a lower bound on the $T$-count of every diagonal gate in the third level of the Clifford hierarchy, the isotropy floor, computable by Gaussian elimination. It is never below the stabilizer nullity $
u$ and reaches $2
u+1$ on non-Clifford gates whose phase is purely cubic. No bound that also holds for circuits with measurement and feedforward can do this, since such circuits implement CCZ ($
u=3$) with four $T$ gates and the layer with $4m$, where the floor gives seven and $6m+1$. The floor also recovers Campbell and Howard's count $4m+3$ for a fan-out of Toffolis. On the output of PyZX's TODD-based optimizer, relative to its Hadamard placement, it certifies $193$ of $311$ phase-polynomial blocks $T$-optimal once repeated parities are merged (at the best of five optimizer seeds), against $113$ for nullity, including $37$ of the $72$ blocks too large for exhaustive search.
item.dc:creator: Arul Rhik Mazumder

item.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.02471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within $2~\mathrm{nm}$ of one another, so the main value of the max--min calculation here is a quantitative performance certificate rather than a large geometric redesign. A full finite-slab calculation and an alternative published GaAs response change the reported pressures by at most $1.60\times10^{-3}\%$ and $4.44\times10^{-2}\%$, respectively. These results establish a reproducible design bound for bilateral nonequilibrium repulsion under dimensional, drive, reflector, and optical-model variations.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed R. Khodja, Belkacem E. Khodja

item.title: Fault tolerance of quantum circuits with tensor networks and symplectic geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.03429v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an operator-algebraic framework for analyzing fault tolerance in quantum circuits and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for exact recovery of the ideal computation under a prescribed noise model. For prescribed circuit families and noise models, we derive a semidefinite program (SDP) based test whose infeasibility certifies that there does not exist any recovery map restoring its intended operation. For non-adaptive stabilizer circuits, analyzing the stabilizer symmetries of its components with symplectic geometry, we obtain closed-form detection and logical-effect matrices that characterize circuit distance algebraically. Applied to a finite Hastings--Haah honeycomb Floquet-code circuit, these matrices certify the dynamical encoding of two logical qubits and distance four under Pauli noise including measurement errors. Using these matrices, we then derive MacWilliams identities for circuit weight enumerators and obtain linear-programming (LP) upper bounds on circuit distance. Output-code constraints give additional Singleton-like bounds. Under independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) depolarizing noise, the weight enumerators determine decoder failure probabilities and yield upper bounds on circuit pseudothresholds. Finally, we derive LP distance bounds for families of flag syndrome-extraction circuits specified by their CNOT orderings, by incorporating the $t$-flag criterion as additional linear constraints to the distance-bounding LP. An analytical CSS Hamming-code benchmark yields a tight distance-three bound attained by the Chao--Reichardt one-flag construction.
item.dc:creator: Soham Ghosh, Holger Boche, Andrew Tanggara

item.title: Universal Bounds for Out-of-Distribution Unitary Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.03690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How much can the action of an unknown unitary dynamics on one family of states reveal about its action elsewhere? We develop a general framework for out-of-distribution quantum dynamics learning based on the first and second moments of the input distribution. These define a notion of the bias and expressivity of an ensemble, which together control generalization between arbitrary mixed-state training and testing distributions. Our framework shows that only studying the action of a unitary on random real states can learn its action on random complex states, that tensor products of unbiased pure-state ensembles preserve expressivity, and that single-qubit risks are independent of bias. It also recovers earlier locally scrambling results as loose special cases and yields tight product-to-Haar bounds. We conclude with a series of no-go results and limited generalization bounds for learning certain channels, which further serve to underscore the distinctive role of unitarity in enabling out-of-distribution generalization.
item.dc:creator: Joachim Favre, Armando Angrisani, Zo\"e Holmes

item.title: Q-MERGE: Parallelising Quantum State Preparation for Large-Scale Classical Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.04247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum processing of classical data fundamentally relies on efficiently mapping classical datasets onto the amplitudes of quantum states. Preparing large amplitude-encoded states, however, remains a major bottleneck in quantum computing. In this paper, we introduce a novel state-preparation framework we call Q-MERGE, that addresses this bottleneck by partitioning a large target state into $M$ $n$-qubit segments, preparing these segments independently and in parallel, and then coherently combining them into a single amplitude-encoded state using SELECT-SWAP operations and measurement. Q-MERGE is agnostic to the segment-level preparation method, allowing existing techniques to be applied to smaller subproblems while providing a tunable trade-off between circuit depth and qubit count. With mid-circuit measurement and preparation-register reuse, the required ancilla qubits can be reduced from O(Mn) to O(n). Applied to a real-world $32 x 1024$ ultrasound dataset, Q-MERGE achieves an infidelity of $3.5 x 10^{-9}$, compared with $6.2 x 10^{-3}$ for direct preparation using the same underlying method, a more than six orders of magnitude improvement at equal CNOT circuit depth. We demonstrate its feasibility experimentally with a 53 qubit circuit comprised of 954 1-qubit gates and 478 2-qubit gates, on the Quantinuum System Model H2 trapped-ion quantum computer. The prepared state is validated using shadow-overlap tomography. Numerical analysis of Haar-random states indicates consistent success probability for up to $M=10^7$ segments, supporting the scalability of Q-MERGE for encoding massive classical datasets.
item.dc:creator: Archie Butterworth, Jens Renders, Jingbo Wang

item.title: Exact Clifford Optimality for Two-Sided Locally Randomized Classical Shadows
item.description: arXiv:2610.04621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entangling measurements can reduce the cost of learning many-body correlations. We consider classical shadows in which a fixed unitary on a $k$-qubit region is sandwiched between two layers of random single-qubit Clifford gates, and ask which middle unitary best estimates Pauli strings with full support on the region. Combining symplectic support counting with a constraint from operator-size parity, we prove that within this architecture the minimum squared shadow norm over all Clifford middle unitaries is $C_k^{\rm opt}=4\cdot 9^k/(3\cdot 5^k+3^k-6)$ for odd $k$ and $C_k^{\rm opt}=4\cdot 9^k/(3\cdot 5^k-3^k+2)$ for even $k$. A dual-axis rotation circuit $U_*$ attains this minimum for every $k$. Asymptotically $C_k^{\rm opt}\simeq(4/3)\cdot(9/5)^k$: the exponential base of Wu et al.'s contractive unitary is optimal, and the prefactor improves from $2$ to $4/3$. For $1\leq k\leq7$, exact certificates show that $U_*$ is optimal over the entire unitary group $\mathrm U(2^k)$, and we conjecture that this holds for every $k$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaotian Nie, Tao Zhang, Yadong Wu, Linghui Chen

item.title: Adiabatic tracking and geometric schedules for classical and quantum Gibbs-state preparation
item.description: arXiv:2610.06268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a discrete adiabatic framework for Gibbs-state preparation in classical and quantum optimisation algorithms. For finite time-inhomogeneous reversible Markov chains, we derive a tracking theorem that bounds the distance between the evolving distribution and the instantaneous stationary state. The bound combines contraction of accumulated error with the new error generated as the stationary distribution changes. For Gibbs paths, it yields explicit step-complexity bounds and an effective tracking metric determined by the spectral gap and equilibrium energy fluctuations. The associated constant-speed schedule minimizes the metric-energy functional and, in the small-gap regime, takes the form $\dot\beta\propto\delta(\beta)/V(\beta)$, where $V(\beta)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\beta}(E)}$. We then apply the discrete quantum adiabatic theorem to temperature-dependent Szegedy quantum walks, whose eigenphase gap satisfies $\Delta_w=\Theta(\sqrt{\delta_+})$, with $\delta_+$ the underlying Markov kernel's right spectral gap. Under uniform bounds on the discrete operator variation and suitable spectral and path-integral assumptions, gap-adapted schedules give a sufficient fixed-accuracy cost of $O(\delta_{+,\min}^{-1/2})$. This gives a quadratic improvement in gap dependence relative to the classical inverse-gap relaxation scale under the stated assumptions. Numerical tests on a solvable two-state model and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick instances compare tracking and final preparation errors and investigate the transfer of schedules from smaller to larger systems.
item.dc:creator: Pedro C. S. Costa, Mauro E. S. Morales, Dong An, Kaur Kristjuhan

item.title: Optimal GHZ extraction from MABK violations
item.description: arXiv:2610.08516v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the least Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability compatible with a Mermin-Ardehali-Belinskii-Klyshko (MABK) Bell score for every $n\geq3$. Extractability is the largest squared overlap with a GHZ state obtainable by separate local quantum channels. Between the biseparable bound and the quantum maximum, its exact minimum is the affine interpolation from one half to one. This proves the bound conjectured for six or more parties. The result holds for arbitrary binary measurements and density operators on tensor products of finite- or infinite-dimensional local spaces. We also determine the exact minimum for qubits, which is strictly higher at every interior score. One qutrit and qubits elsewhere attain the unrestricted minimum with measurements fixed as the score varies and, at interior scores, realize the smallest product of ranks of the local reduced states among states attaining that minimum. For $n\geq4$, the attaining state with this rank product is unique at each interior score, up to local isometries and party permutations. On one qutrit and qubits elsewhere, for $n\geq4$ and scores a fixed fraction away from both endpoints, a sufficiently small excess of extractability above the minimum controls trace-norm distance to the attaining state of the same score, up to local unitaries. The dependence is of square-root order, with optimal exponent and explicit constants depending only on that fraction, uniformly in $n$. Equality and stability concern actual extractability; identical Bell statistics can accompany different extractabilities.
item.dc:creator: Avraham Kreindel (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Redundant Records of the Past: Unifying Quantum Darwinism and Decoherent Histories
item.description: arXiv:2610.09845v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There exist two different paradigms for records in isolated quantum systems: decoherent histories (which determines which past events leave formal records) and quantum Darwinism (which determines which current events get redundantly recorded). Neither one implies the other, and connections between the two are scarcely investigated. We unify quantum Darwinism and decoherent histories based on the insight that only redundant records about past events matter. The resulting framework of past redundancy encompasses quantum Darwinism when applied to events at the current time, and it implies the probability sum rule or decoherence of histories. The Bhattacharyya coefficient (or fidelity) plays an important role to establish this connection. Importantly, various examples show that past redundancy is a more widespread phenomenon than the fine-tuned models necessary for quantum Darwinism suggest. We thus arrive at a richer picture in which redundancy can be caused by mechanisms different from quantum Darwinism (such as macroevents or cascade structures), which emphasizes that redundancy is necessary but not sufficient for objectivity, and which, overall, allows to realistically investigate the question: how generic is redundancy in nature?
item.dc:creator: Philipp Strasberg

item.title: Exact value and rigidity of the $2\times3$ magic rectangle
item.description: arXiv:2610.12001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $2\times3$ magic rectangle is a nonlocal game in which two players match entries subject to incompatible parity constraints. Its quantum value was suggested by numerical bounds and known quantum random access codes. We prove that this value is $(1+\sqrt{2/3})/2$ and classify all optimal strategies in arbitrary finite local dimensions, allowing general measurements: up to local isometries and ancillary systems, each contains a maximally entangled pair of four-dimensional systems with fixed measurements on the local state supports. The same value holds for commuting-operator strategies and for the almost-quantum relaxation, confirming the Adamson--Wallden conjecture for this rectangle. For finite-dimensional magic-square strategies, the largest score compatible with perfect prediction of Alice's complete first row by an adversary with quantum side information is one third plus two thirds of the rectangle value. We classify the strategies attaining this threshold with perfect prediction and give linear-order upper and lower bounds on one minus the best compatible guessing probability above it. The rectangle value is also the optimal average success probability of finite-dimensional three-bit random access codes that hide the full input parity, and we classify all optimal codes.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Barouch Essayag (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: An Instability of the Quantum Markov Length
item.description: arXiv:2610.12929v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Markov length, the length scale governing the exponential decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) in a quantum many-body state, has proven useful for characterizing mixed-state phases of matter. Nevertheless, we show that a state's Markov length is not generally stable under weak local channels. The failure of stability occurs already at a pure product state. We demonstrate this explicitly in a one-dimensional fermionic chain, where a fine-tuned depth-two circuit of nearest-neighbor Gaussian channels maps the vacuum to a state whose CMI decays \emph{algebraically} and whose Markov length is therefore infinite, even when the channels are taken arbitrarily close to the identity. The algebraic decay is rooted in the nonanalyticity of the von Neumann entropy at rank-deficient density operators. We exhibit an analogous instability on an ordinary qubit chain. More generally, we show that the Markov length is unstable in any translation-invariant state with even a single rank-deficient reduced density operator. These results pose a challenge to recent definitions of mixed-state phase equivalence based on the Markov length.
item.dc:creator: David C. Newsom, Michael Levin

item.title: Finite-Size Limits of Adaptive Pauli Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2610.13652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The expectation values of a predetermined set of Pauli observables can be predicted using only a few copies of a quantum state. However, when later observables depend on earlier predictions, how the system size constrains the required number of copies remains unclear. We use classical interactive fingerprinting codes to establish this constraint. A compact Pauli-parity encoding embeds the fingerprinting interaction into the quantum prediction task, allowing any quantum prediction mechanism on the constructed diagonal states to be simulated by a classical response strategy subject to the same information constraints. We show that accurate prediction from too few copies would violate the guarantees of the fingerprinting code. For $n$ qubits and $M$ adaptively chosen Pauli observables, requiring all predictions to be simultaneously accurate to a fixed additive error with probability at least $2/3$ yields the worst-case lower bound $N^*(n,M)=\Omega(\sqrt{\min\{n,M\}})$ on the required number of copies. For $M\le n$, this lower bound matches known upper bounds. In particular, $n$ adaptive predictions require $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$ copies, whereas the same number of predetermined queries requires only $O(\log n)$ copies. This separation persists even for diagonal states and commuting observables.
item.dc:creator: Luofei Wang, Boyu Liu, Zihe Wang, Zhangqi Yin

item.title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
item.description: arXiv:2610.15791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Wu

item.title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.21928v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under indepen dent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.
item.dc:creator: Si-Yu Zhang, Meng-Long Song, Hai-Tao Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang

item.title: Local distinguishability of five quadripartite orthogonal product states
item.description: arXiv:2610.29622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The local distinguishability of five bipartite and tripartite orthogonal product states (OPSs) has been effectively resolved, while that of five quadripartite OPSs has not yet been effectively addressed. In this paper, we give the local distinguishability of five quadripartite OPSs, where any two of these five states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. Based on the vectors of the numbers of pairwise orthogonality relations, we classify different sets of five quadripartite OPSs into nine categories, which correspond to 371 distinct orthogonality graphs. We show that the sets of five quadripartite OPSs corresponding to 355 of the 371 cases can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), whereas the sets of five quadripartite OPSs for the remaining 16 cases cannot exactly distinguished by LOCC. Our results enrich the theory of nonlocality for sets of OPSs.
item.dc:creator: Guang-Bao Xu, Jie Zhan, Yu-Guang Yang, Dong-Huan Jiang

item.title: On the Role of Problem Structure in Single-Layer QAOA
item.description: arXiv:2610.30511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Problem structure is widely regarded as a key factor influencing the performance of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), yet it often remains an informal notion without a precise mathematical characterization. In this work, we introduce a mathematical framework for characterizing problem structure from the perspective of target-state amplification in single-layer QAOA. We show that this structure can be represented by a joint probability distribution capturing the relationship between problem costs and mixer-dependent dynamics. We identify the statistical dependence encoded in this distribution as a measure of problem structure, through which necessary conditions for exponential amplification can be established. We establish a mean--max non-separation bound connecting parameter-averaged probabilities to their variational maxima. For NPO-PB problems with polynomially many distinct mixer eigenvalues, these probabilities exhibit the same scaling up to polynomial factors, allowing the exponential scaling of optimal amplification to be characterized without explicit parameter optimization. Beyond this characterization, mean--max non-separation also identifies regimes in which random-parameter QAOA can match the sampling guarantees of variationally trained QAOA. We further derive a matrix representation of the parameter-averaged probability that separates structural information from mixer dynamics, providing insight into the mechanisms governing probability amplification and its exponential suppression relative to the mixer capacity. These mechanisms are illustrated through analytically tractable examples involving transverse field and Grover mixers.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Andris Ambainis

item.title: A simple proof of unitary parallelization via port-based teleportation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Port-based teleportation (PBT) is a variant of quantum teleportation that does not require corrections on the teleported state: starting with $N$ shared EPR states, Alice can teleport a qudit to Bob by performing a measurement on her system and informing Bob which of his $N$ `ports' to retrieve the state, up to infidelity decaying with $N$. Existing efficient quantum circuits of PBT rely on representation theory tools such as the Schur transform. In this note, we report an elementary efficient circuit for PBT, which has depth $\operatorname{polylog}(N,d)$. As a corollary, this gives a simple proof that all $n$-qubit unitaries can be parallelized to $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ depth, recovering a recent result due to Nehoran--Slote--Yuen and OpenAI.
item.dc:creator: Anurag Anshu, Quynh T. Nguyen

item.title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2610.35227v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universal fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers are expected to require millions of physical qubits; yet extending the prevailing dedicated-control-line paradigm to this scale would exceed the wiring density and cooling-power budget of dilution refrigerators. Microwave frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) revolutionized classical communications by enabling many independent channels to share common transmission infrastructure. Translating this principle to superconducting quantum control, however, requires an all-microwave architecture and experimental validation of frequency-multiplexed gate control. Recent work in quantum error correction has demonstrated microwave-based readout, single-qubit gates and leakage suppression, whereas two-qubit gates remain predominantly driven by unipolar pulses and thus constitute the missing element of an all-microwave architecture. Here, we propose a periodically extensible hybrid multiplexing framework in which all gate operations are frequency-division multiplexed using polychromatic microwave pulses and band-pass filters, thereby reducing the required control-line count by one to two orders of magnitude. In a 1:4 demonstration, we achieve average errors of $(6.4\pm0.2)\times10^{-3}$ for parallel FDM CZ gates and $(10.6\pm0.2)\times10^{-4}$ for parallel FDM $XY(\pi/2)$ gates, without statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation. Together with on-chip DC sources, this FDM-based gate-control scheme completes the last missing module in a scalable multiplexed-control architecture toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing.
item.dc:creator: Dayu Li, Naibin Zhou, Zhiyuan Chen, Zihua Chen, Yu Xu, Yuan Li, Daojin Fan, Wenhao Chu, Xiawei Chen, Hui Deng, Jiacheng Gui, Linyin Hong, Bo Fan, Weiping Lin, Haonan Zou, Haoxin Lou, Xintao Zhao, Sirui Cao, Ying Chong, Qingling Zhu, Chen Wang, Yisen Hu, Kaili Zhang, Feifan Su, Haibin Zhang, Jianghan Yin, Yajie Du, Yinan Jiang, Haoping Luo, Weifeng Yang, Jiafei Wang, Jin Lin, Futian Liang, Hao Rong, Kai Yan, Ming Gong, Jinjin Li, Maliang Liu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Shaowei Li, Xiaobo Zhu, Jian-Wei Pan

item.title: GAnnET: A principled approach to automatically annotating charge stability diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2312.11206v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum-dot (QD) arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing. However, their large configuration spaces and inherent measurement noise make device tuning time consuming and difficult to scale. Although machine-learning (ML) approaches for automated tuning have proliferated rapidly, a fair comparison of methods remains limited by inconsistent metrics and a lack of standardized labeled datasets. Here, we introduce Geometry-Informed ANNotator for Electrostatic Topologies (GAnnET), a physics- and geometry-informed algorithm that automatically generates probabilistic state labels for charge stability diagrams (CSDs) of double-QD systems. GAnnET constructs local geometric models of CSD structure and combines them into a global state map with calibrated confidence, eliminating the need for manual annotation. We validate GAnnET on simulated and experimental CSDs and demonstrate consistent labeling suitable for ML training and benchmarking. By enabling reproducible annotation of experimental data, GAnnET supports community benchmarking and scalable automated QD operation.
item.dc:creator: Brian Weber, Justyna P. Zwolak

item.title: Chiral Geometric Qubit in a Frustrated Molecular Spin Triangle
item.description: arXiv:2501.11964v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spin frustration in antiferromagnetically coupled triangles creates states distinguished by chirality, offering a molecular route to encoded quantum operations. Here, we show how scalar chirality and geometric phases arise in the ground doublet of a spin-$1/2$ triangle. A Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction establishes the chirality of the states, while broken $C_3$ symmetry allows these states to acquire geometric phases. We show how to encode a qubit in states of opposite scalar chirality and opposite geometric phases and implement a geometric $Z$ gate that cancels the relative dynamical phase, making it insensitive to pulse-duration errors. As an example of such a chiral geometric qubit, we investigate a Cu$_3$-based paramagnetic molecular magnet, using broken-symmetry density functional theory and multireference spin--orbit calculations to estimate the strengths of the exchange and DM interactions. The results show that such paramagnetic molecules could serve as tunable platforms for implementing chiral geometric qubits.
item.dc:creator: Aman Ullah, Ziqi Hu, Juan Arag\'o, Sergey A. Varganov, Alejandro Gaita-Ari\~no

item.title: Quantum noise spectroscopy of superconducting dynamics in a cuprate thin film
item.description: arXiv:2502.04439v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterizing the low-energy dynamics of quantum materials is crucial for understanding strongly correlated electronic states, yet remains experimentally challenging, particularly in two-dimensional systems. Here, we leverage nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as a non-invasive quantum sensor to study thin-film Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$ (BSCCO), revealing several distinct dynamical phenomena across the superconducting phase diagram. At zero magnetic field and low temperatures, NV depolarization ($T_1$) spectroscopy captures GHz-scale noise from nodal quasiparticle excitations, consistent with Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) mean-field theory. Near the critical temperature $T_c \approx 90$ K, supercurrent-fluctuation-induced noise sharply reduces $T_1$. By analyzing the temperature scaling of $T_1$, we observe clear deviations from mean-field prediction, reflecting the importance of order parameter fluctuations and enabling the determination of critical exponents. Under a small magnetic field, a broad and asymmetric reduction of $T_1$ unveils a liquid-like phase of mobile vortices. NV decoherence ($T_2$) spectroscopy further probes MHz-scale noise and reveals complex vortex-solid fluctuations well below $T_c$. Our results establish quantum noise spectroscopy as a non-invasive probe of superconducting dynamics over frequency and length scales complementary to existing techniques.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyuan Liu, Ruotian Gong, Jaewon Kim, Oriana K. Diessel, Jiajie Cheng, Qiaozhi Xu, Zackary Rehfuss, Xinyi Du, Guanghui He, Abhishek Singh, Yun Suk Eo, Erik A. Henriksen, G. D. Gu, Norman Y. Yao, Francisco Machado, Sheng Ran, Shubhayu Chatterjee, Chong Zu

item.title: The Baby Universe is Fine and the CFT Knows It: On Holography for Closed Universes
item.description: arXiv:2507.10649v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Big bang/big crunch closed universes can be realized in AdS/CFT, even though they lack asymptotically AdS boundaries. With enough bulk entanglement, the bulk Hilbert space of a closed universe can be holographically encoded in the CFT. We clarify the relation of this encoding to observer-clone proposals and refute recent arguments about the breakdown of semiclassical physics in such spaces. In the limit of no bulk entanglement, the holographic encoding breaks down. The oft-cited one-dimensional nature of the closed universe Hilbert space represents the limitation of the external (CFT) Hilbert space to access the quantum information in the closed universe, similar to the limitations imposed on observers outside a perfectly isolated quantum lab. We advocate that the CFT nevertheless continues to determine the physical properties of the closed universe in this regime, showing how to interpret this relationship in terms of a final state projection in the closed universe. We provide a dictionary between the final state wavefunction and CFT data. We propose a model of the emergence of an arrow of time in the universe with a given initial or final state projection. Finally, we show that the conventional EFT in the closed universe, without any projection, can be recovered as a maximally ignorant description of the final state. This conventional EFT is encoded in CFT data, and it can be probed by computing coarse-grained observables. We provide an example of one such observable. Taken together, these results amount to a clean bill of health for baby universes born of AdS/CFT.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Antonini, Pratik Rath, Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, Alejandro Vilar L\'opez

item.title: Quantum-inspired space-time PDE solver and dynamic mode decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2510.21767v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The numerical solution of time-dependent PDEs posed over the combined space-time domain, instead of treating time sequentially, leads to space-time methods. Treating time as another spatial dimension allows parallelization across time and simultaneous adaptivity in spatial and temporal discretizations. However, space-time formulations suffer from the curse of dimensionality due to the (d+1)-dimensional domain. Time-series forecasting methods, such as dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), also suffer the same scaling for storing and processing measurement data. In this work, we investigate whether quantum-inspired tensor network methods can mitigate this curse for both solving PDEs and data-driven modeling. We formulate a space-time matrix product state (MPS) encoding to represent either the space-time solution or time-series data. Using this representation, we develop a unified framework that combines an MPS space-time PDE solver with an MPS-DMD algorithm. We benchmark our MPS space-time solver for linear and nonlinear PDEs in both (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions, including non-diffusive regimes such as shockwave formation and Allen-Cahn phase separation.
